issue: After an automatic upgrade, all network rules were removed and caused a 24h duration outage of all their Cilium protected Kubernetes clusters in all their regions and cloud providers.
root_cause: The root cause was an automatic security update to systemd on March 8, 2023, at 06:00 UTC. This update triggered a latent interaction in the network stack, causing systemd-networkd to forcibly delete routing rules managed by the Cilium Container Network Interface (CNI) plugin.
solution: All services were operational by March 9, 08:58 UTC, and the incident was fully resolved, including historical data backfill, by March 10, 06:25 UTC. This update triggered a latent interaction in the network stack, causing systemd-networkd to forcibly delete routing rules managed by the Cilium Container Network Interface (CNI) plugin.

issue: A staged Kubernetes upgrade of CircleCI's main production cluster left `kube-proxy` and `kubelet` at incompatible versions.
root_cause: The change between versions altered the format of `kube-proxy`'s `iptables` rulesets, so as pods churned and `Endpoints` objects changed, `kube-proxy`'s `Proxier.syncProxyRules ` (an `iptables-save` / `iptables-restore` read-modify-write) repeatedly hit "Sync failed" errors, leaving the per-node iptables in a corrupted state and silently breaking service-to-service routing across the cluster.
solution: Recovery required a full node-by-node cluster restart and triggered two follow-on incidents.

issue: Login page and dashboard briefly show odd cross-account data before the site goes fully down for maintenance.
root_cause: Queues used to hold requests and responses for an AI system's cache became corrupted and got out of sequence, which meant some responses were served to the wrong user, unintentionally revealing details like another user's activity history and some billing information.
solution: Took the affected system down while the sequencing bug in the cache/queue handling was fixed, and notified affected users about what categories of information may have been exposed to someone else.

issue: ChatGPT offline; users exposed to other active users' chat titles and payment details.
root_cause: A bug in the redis-py Redis client library caused connections to be recycled with incorrect session context under heavy load.
solution: Patched the redis-py library to clear connection state upon context validation failure.

issue: OpenAI Moderation endpoint requests experiencing high latency and HTTP 504 timeouts.
root_cause: A database scale-up in the moderation policy registry caused write deadlocks on the moderation servers.
solution: Aborted the policy scale-up and optimized database lock parameters in the moderation service.

issue: Google Cloud VMware Engine (GCVE) customer clusters were automatically deleted, causing permanent data loss.
root_cause: Initial GCVE provisioning was done using a legacy option with a fixed-term contract that lacked automatic renewal, triggering automated deletion workflows at the end of the term.
solution: Restored customer workloads from external backups and updated internal provisioning accounts to prevent automatic expiration of infrastructure services.

issue: New authorizations and deployments failing platform-wide with a database-level error, unrelated to any application code change.
root_cause: A foreign key column was defined with a smaller integer data type than the primary key column it referenced. When the primary key's values exceeded what the smaller foreign-key type could hold, inserts began failing with an overflow error, blocking creation of new authorizations, downstream, new deployments.
solution: Corrected the mismatched column data type so the foreign key could represent the full range of primary key values, resolving the overflow and restoring the ability to create authorizations and deployments.

issue: Heroku Connect sync between Salesforce and Postgres failing.
root_cause: An API update in Salesforce modified field serialization order, breaking the parsing logic in Heroku Connect.
solution: Released a client parser hotfix that supports dynamic field indexing, and restarted sync workers.

issue: Elevated error rates and timeout latencies for AWS Lambda invocations in US-East-1.
root_cause: A configuration deployment to Lambda routing proxies caused CPU starvation under peak load.
solution: Rolled back the proxy configuration changes and scaled routing nodes to handle load.

issue: SMS and push notifications delayed for several minutes.
root_cause: A downstream SMS aggregator network connection degraded, backing up notification dispatcher buffers.
solution: Switched traffic to backup SMS providers and increased dispatcher queue capacities.

issue: API calls unexpectedly getting rate-limited far more often than usual after a routine maintenance window.
root_cause: Maintenance on the API token-management system inadvertently changed how token validation interacted with the rate-limiting system, causing much stricter rate-limit enforcement to be applied broadly, including to calls that should have been exempt.
solution: Reverted the token-validation/rate-limiting interaction to the correct behavior; added monitoring so this kind of enforcement-rate spike is caught automatically instead of relying on customer reports.

issue: OpenAI Fine-Tuning API jobs failing to start or stuck in execution.
root_cause: A thread pool exhaustion in the fine-tuning orchestrator blocked job schedule queues.
solution: Increased fine-tuning orchestrator thread pool sizes and scaled computing nodes.

issue: All crate downloads from crates.io failed for 13 minutes, causing millions of failed cargo build requests.
root_cause: A deployment introduced a bug in the download URL generation logic, causing it to return malformed URLs for all download requests.
solution: Rolled back the deployment and added unit tests covering download URL generation.

issue: On July 25th, 2023, we experienced a total Honeycomb outage.
root_cause: It impacted all user-facing components from 1:40 p.m. UTC to 2:48 p.m. UTC, during which no data could be processed or accessed.
solution: The full details of incident triage process is covered in here.

issue: ChatGPT Plugin Directory unavailable or returning connection errors.
root_cause: A bug in the plugin directory search service triggered query parsing infinite loops under specific text symbols.
solution: Patched the directory search query parser code and restarted search API nodes.

issue: 1.1.1.1 public DNS resolver returning SERVFAIL responses.
root_cause: DNSSEC validation failed in resolver software after a key rotation mismatch caused invalid signatures.
solution: Temporarily disabled DNSSEC checks, synced keys, and re-enabled validation.

issue: ChatGPT API and web interface experiencing high error rates and timeouts.
root_cause: A distributed denial of service (DDoS) attack saturated the edge proxies and gateway controllers.
solution: Implemented stricter WAF rate-limiting rules and isolated traffic from known malicious IP blocks.

issue: Multiple SimpleDB storage nodes lost power simultaneously in one US-East data center.
root_cause: The lock service de-registered them rapidly, which spiked load and pushed handshake latencies above SimpleDB's too-aggressive handshake timeout. Healthy storage and metadata nodes failed their handshakes, removed themselves from the cluster, and couldn't rejoin because the metadata nodes that would authorize them had also taken themselves out.
solution: Recovery required manually raising the handshake timeout and restarting metadata nodes.

issue: A "network disruption" caused metadata services to experience load that caused response times to exceed timeout values, causing storage nodes to take themselves down.
root_cause: This disruption caused storage servers to query the internal metadata service for their membership assignments. The root cause was a combination of factors.
solution: Nodes that took themselves down continued to retry, ensuring that load on metadata services couldn't decrease.

issue: ChatGPT users exposed to other active chat session data.
root_cause: A race condition in session mapping logic during high traffic volume peaks mixed up user context keys.
solution: Implemented strict session-isolation scopes and refactored thread locks on connection managers.

issue: GitHub Actions workflow queues delayed and runner communication failing.
root_cause: Redis connection limits on the orchestrator were exceeded due to a connection leak introduced in a worker service deployment.
solution: Rolled back the worker deployment, terminated leaky connections, and raised limits.

issue: GitHub write operations degraded, and repository updates delayed for several hours.
root_cause: A network partition between data centers triggered automated primary promotion, but the chosen replica had stale replication streams.
solution: Manually forced failover to the correct database node and restarted write operations.

issue: A Kinesis cell newly migrated to a new architecture had an unusually high number of very low-throughput shards.
root_cause: The cell management system distributed the shards unevenly, so a few hosts ended up handling huge numbers of shards and produced abnormally large status messages. The system misinterpreted slow status messages as host failures, kicked off a redistribution storm, and overloaded the secure-connection provisioning subsystem.
solution: CloudWatch Logs, S3 event notifications, Firehose, ECS, Lambda, Redshift, MWAA, and Glue all degraded for ~7 hours.

issue: Site-wide read outage after a routine database configuration rollout.
root_cause: A configuration change rolled out to production databases changed how hosts responded to routing-service health checks. The health-check system incorrectly marked the read-only endpoint as unhealthy, taking it out of rotation even though the databases themselves were fine.
solution: Reverted the configuration change to restore correct health-check responses; read traffic resumed within the hour once the endpoint was marked healthy again.

issue: Git clones and pushes failing intermittently due to file server errors.
root_cause: A file storage array array controller hardware failure led to data corruption on primary volumes.
solution: Activated secondary controller paths and synchronized volumes from replica logs.

issue: GitHub Gists and Pages unavailable, returning database errors.
root_cause: An unoptimized search query triggered database write locks, exhausting active connection pools.
solution: Optimized the query, terminated locking transactions, and added database rate limits.

issue: Webhook delivery delays of up to several hours.
root_cause: A queue queue capacity limit bug in the webhook broker caused delivery worker starvation.
solution: Pushed a hotfix to expand queue capacities and scaled consumer nodes.

issue: Long outage of a data-center-hosted service; on-site staff unable to resolve it quickly on their own.
root_cause: A control-plane and analytics system running across three physically separate data centers relied on a colocation provider's backup power arrangement. When utility power was interrupted, the backup generator arrangement didn't behave as expected, and it took considerable time to get clarity from the colocation provider on why, since key technical details about their power failover setup weren't fully documented or communicated in advance.
solution: Worked with the colocation provider to restore power and bring systems back online, then pushed to get full documentation of the provider's power failover design and clearer communication commitments for any future incident of this kind.

issue: New feature under heavy testing causes hangs and crashes in the test suite, but only intermittently and only with the new code path.
root_cause: A months-long performance rewrite of core I/O handling introduced a native code path (needed because the new high-performance async I/O API wasn't available in managed code). The new code had a subtle interlocking bug that only manifested as a race condition under certain timing conditions, making it hang or crash unpredictably rather than failing consistently.
solution: Caught during testing rather than in production; resolved by isolating and fixing the specific interlock logic in the native code path, after extended debugging effort by multiple engineers.

issue: Dashboard, mobile app, and API all briefly unavailable at the same time shortly after a database version upgrade.
root_cause: After a Postgres major-version upgrade, an audit-logging extension that had passed staging tests was re-enabled in production. A routine table-creation migration triggered a pathological interaction with that extension, which hung while holding critical locks and ignored timeout signals, blocking other database operations across multiple products at once.
solution: Restarted the primary database to forcibly break the deadlock (a short hard outage), then removed the problematic extension entirely rather than attempting to reconfigure it.

issue: GitHub API returning HTTP 503 errors and blocking Git operations.
root_cause: A faulty routing policy deployed to the API gateway caused request routing redirect loops.
solution: Reverted the API gateway routing configuration and restarted edge proxies.

issue: Gist read/write operations experiencing intermittent failures.
root_cause: Redis session cluster for Gists became saturated due to a connection leak in Gist client components.
solution: Patched the Gist client wrapper to correctly release connections and restarted the session cluster.

issue: Repository archiving and download requests failing with HTTP 504 gateway timeouts.
root_cause: Storage mount disk latency spiked in the archive storage array because of a disk controller card failure.
solution: Replaced the failed storage array controller card and synchronized data streams.

issue: Legitimate customer traffic being blocked by the web application firewall with no recent deploys to explain it.
root_cause: A gap in access controls allowed a change to be made to a firewall configuration outside of the normal infrastructure-as-code pipeline. Because the change wasn't recorded in the deployment history, on-call responders spent significant time chasing unrelated leads (like recent code deploys and CORS errors) before automated drift detection revealed the untracked firewall change as the real cause.
solution: Reverted the out-of-band firewall change and tightened access controls so that infrastructure changes outside the standard pipeline are blocked or immediately flagged.

issue: CircleCI build workflow triggering and job scheduling suffered major delays following a database upgrade.
root_cause: A major-version blue/green database upgrade succeeded, but a secondary update immediately after rendered the database query optimizer statistics stale. Without indexes, all queries ran full table scans against disk.
solution: Re-promoted the blue (old) database to quickly restore operations, and adjusted the migration sequence to run ANALYZE immediately post-cutover.

issue: GitHub API Gateway returning high TLS handshake timeouts for developer queries.
root_cause: A configuration drift in API gateway SSL cipher settings caused CPU exhaustion on load balancers during peak traffic.
solution: Reverted the SSL cipher configuration changes to the standard set.

issue: Issues, Projects, and Milestones creation failing with internal database write locks.
root_cause: A routine database index optimization job on the main tickets table acquired exclusive tables locks under active load.
solution: Terminated the optimization job, optimized locking queries, and deferred indexes build.

issue: A policy change containing blank fields triggered a null pointer exception in Service Control, Google's API management and control plane system.
root_cause: The code path that failed was not feature flag protected and lacked proper error handling. When the policy data replicated globally, it caused Service Control binaries to crash loop across all regions. While a red-button fix was deployed within 40 minutes, larger regions like us-central-1 experienced extended recovery times (up to 2h 40m) due to a thundering herd problem when Service Control tasks restarted, overloading the underlying Spanner infrastructure.
solution: The incident affected Google and Google Cloud APIs globally, with recovery times varying by product architecture.

issue: GitHub Actions orchestrator experiencing slow run initiations.
root_cause: A memory leak in the runner orchestration Go service led to slow garbage collection sweeps, increasing scheduling times.
solution: Rolled back the orchestrator service release to a stable version and debugged the leak.

issue: Webhook notifications and integrations processing delayed by up to 30 minutes.
root_cause: A database schema change in the integration metadata table locked query execution paths in the delivery worker broker.
solution: Rolled back the schema change and rescheduled the update for off-peak hours.

issue: GitHub Pages deployment pipelines stuck in queued state.
root_cause: A certificate renewal task hung in a locked state, blocking subsequent deployment queue consumers.
solution: Killed the blocked renewal task, restarted deployment worker services, and added execution timeouts.

issue: Pull Requests pages loading slowly or failing to render diffs.
root_cause: A high volume of concurrent commits to monorepos triggered lock queues on git file servers.
solution: Adjusted PR diff-rendering concurrency limits and enabled aggressive diff caching rules.

issue: SSH and HTTPS Git authentication failing intermittently for over an hour.
root_cause: A memory allocation failure in the internal user-session cache cluster led to authentication lookups falling back to slow DB paths.
solution: Restarted the affected cache nodes and increased cache cluster RAM allocation limits.

issue: The website for Xubuntu, a derivative of Ubuntu Linux that uses Xfce as its desktop environment, was compromised by an attacker who changed download links to a malicious zip file.
root_cause: The incident was caused by a malicious actor who gained unauthorized access to the WordPress installation maintaining the Xubuntu website.
solution: As a long-term remediation, the Xubuntu team decided to migrate their website to Hugo, a static site generator, to eliminate the type of attack vector exploited.

issue: Widespread cloud service disruption, new connections to a core database service failing region-wide.
root_cause: A latent race condition in the automated DNS-management system for a managed database service caused two internal automation components to overwrite each other's DNS update, ultimately leaving an empty DNS record for the service's regional endpoint. Because so many other services depended on this database for internal coordination, the DNS failure cascaded into compute provisioning and other control-plane systems.
solution: Engineers manually restored the correct DNS records and disabled the automation that caused the conflict while it was fixed. Downstream systems that had accumulated bad state (like stale leases) needed additional manual recovery time even after the DNS issue itself was resolved.

issue: The AWS us-east-1 outage degraded EC2/Lambda/DynamoDB/Route 53, leaving Launchdarkly's US web app, API, and client-side streaming SDKs unable to autoscale and dropping events.
root_cause: The initial phase was triggered by a major AWS us-east-1 outage, which degraded services like EC2, Lambda, DynamoDB, and Route 53. This caused excessive retries from SDKs, overwhelming the streaming service and its load balancer, which then became unresponsive.
solution: After AWS recovered, an internal change meant to shed load reverted flag-delivery to a legacy routing path with cold caches; SDKs hammered the streaming service with retries, the load balancer became unresponsive, and EC2 provisioning issues prevented scale-out, taking server-side streaming globally to ~99% errors and keeping US streaming down for another ~12 hours.

issue: During the AWS us-east-1 outage, incident.io's Google-Cloud-hosted platform mostly held but third-party AWS dependencies cascaded into a complex multi-team response: their telecom provider's outage backed up the on-call notification queue (~30× normal load), their deploy pipeline was wedged because their builder transitively pulled `golang:1.24.9-alpine` from Docker Hub (which runs on AWS), and Postgres dead tuples in the escalation-acquisition index turned scaling up workers into a net throughput regression.
root_cause: Although incident.io's core platform is hosted on Google Cloud, several key services were impacted due to dependencies on AWS-hosted third parties. Specific failures included Scribe being unable to join calls from 07:34 to 10:07 UTC and again from 12:40 to 17:37 UTC due to an AWS-hosted transcription provider.
solution: A traffic-management feature flag also failed to apply globally because of a recent "top 10 orgs by volume" usability tweak.

issue: GitHub Copilot completions experiencing timeouts and failed requests.
root_cause: A configuration drift in the model gateway proxies restricted keep-alive socket reuse, flooding backend clusters.
solution: Corrected the proxy configuration setting and re-aligned keep-alive parameters across regions.

issue: Global CDN and proxy outage after an internal permissions change.
root_cause: A permissions update on an internal analytics database changed how a query returned table metadata, causing it to unexpectedly return duplicate rows. This bloated a configuration file used by the bot-detection system beyond a hard-coded size limit, which crashed the proxy software that handles most customer traffic.
solution: Rolled back to a last-known-good version of the configuration file to restore traffic, then fixed the query and added stricter validation and size limits on generated configuration files before they are distributed network-wide.

issue: Codespaces creation and session loading experiencing elevated latency.
root_cause: Hypervisor host connection limit reached in the primary region due to slow container cleanup routines.
solution: Manually purged idle hypervisor containers and optimized cleanup daemon check frequencies.

issue: All virtual machine provisioning operations (Actions, Codespaces) failed globally for over five hours.
root_cause: A telemetry configuration gap caused security policies to be automatically applied to backend storage accounts, which blocked critical VM metadata access in the underlying cloud provider.
solution: Reverted the auto-applied security policies and added telemetry validation checks to prevent incorrect policy enforcement.

issue: GitHub Package Registry publishing operations delayed or returning HTTP 500 errors.
root_cause: An unindexed metadata lookup query in the registry backend database triggered 100% CPU lock on active read replicas.
solution: Pushed an indexing migration script to the database and scaled up registry replica pools.

issue: API error rates climb steadily over several hours with no single obvious trigger, unlike a typical sudden outage.
root_cause: Frontend traffic increased gradually while a backend database service was already running close to capacity; a database index design concentrated certain metadata on only a few shards, and a short cache expiration time forced frequent database refreshes, so read contention on those few shards grew disproportionately as traffic rose.
solution: According to the incident report, mitigations focused on redistributing the concentrated metadata across more shards and lengthening the cache expiration window to reduce refresh frequency and read contention.
note: This detail appeared inside a third-party aggregator page alongside an unrelated Slack incident; verify against Google's own incident report before relying on it for evaluation.

issue: 13 min read Summary of Windows Azure Service Disruption on Feb 29th, 2012 By The Microsoft Azure Team, view all posts by this author Share Link copied to clipboard!
root_cause: Certificates that were valid for one year were created. Instead of using an appropriate library, someone wrote code that computed one year to be the current date plus one year. On February 29th 2012, this resulted in the creation of certificates with an expiration date of February 29th 2013, which were rejected because of the invalid date. This caused an Azure global outage that lasted for most of a day.
solution: At that point the FC stops all internally initiated software updates and automatic service healing is disabled. To prevent customers from inadvertently causing further impact to their running applications, unsuccessfully scaling-out their applications, and fruitlessly trying to deploy new applications, we disabled service management functionality in all clusters worldwide.

issue: Receiving full sync requests from each redis-slave caused the master to suffer extreme load, resulting in performance degradation of the master and timeouts from redis-slaves to redis-master.
root_cause: In 2013, a temporary network partition in the redis cluster used for billing operations, caused a massive resynchronization from slaves. The overloaded master crashed and when it was restarted, it started up in read-only mode. The auto-recharge component in This resulted in failed transactions from Twilio's auto-recharge service, which unfortunately billed the customers before updating their balance internally. So the auto-recharge system continued to retry the transaction again and again, resulting in multiple charges to customer's credit cards.
solution: Some accounts were suspended as a result of a recharge attempted against a credit card deactivated by the repeated billing. /: Our on-call engineers restarted the redis-master to address the high load.

issue: 2013–09–17 Outage Postmortem Xandr Engineering Follow 6 min read · -- 1 Listen Share On starting at ( America/New_York) the AppNexus platform experienced a technical failure that initially fully halted ad serving and later partially degraded ad serving with the entire incident lasting approximately two and a half hours.
root_cause: A double free revealed by a database update caused all "impression bus" servers to crash simultaneously. This wasn't caught in staging and made it into production because a time delay is required to trigger the bug, and the staging period didn't have a built-in delay.
solution: By ( America/New_York), one engineering team restored enough capacity in our Amsterdam data center (AMS1) to service 50% of Amsterdam’s regular volume of direct transactions. Our engineers restored service in AMS1 using a new snapshot of data from the internal database.

issue: Service disruption at Knight Capital (see incident report).
root_cause: A combination of conflicting deployed versions and re-using a previously used bit caused a $460M loss. See also a longer write-up.
solution: Knight did not have a second technician review this deployment and no one at Knight realized that the Power Peg code had not been removed from the eighth server, nor the new RLP code added. The email messages references SMARS and identified an error as “Power Peg disabled.” there were 97 of these emails sent to Knight personnel.

issue: Incorrect DOWN reports. During the outage we failed to alert on missed snitch check-ins and sent a large number of erroneous failure alerts for healthy snitches.
root_cause: In this case, the unscoped deletion was introduced as part of implementing a suggestion to reduce the number of queries made during an interval change.
solution: We were alerted immediately disabled our alerter process to avoid further confusion. We began diagnosing the cause and at deployed a fix for the unscoped delete.

issue: Stack Exchange Network Status — Outage Postmortem - Here we'll post updates on outages and maintenance windows for the Stack Exchange Network.
root_cause: Backtracking implementation in the underlying regex engine turned out to be very expensive for a particular post leading to health-check failures and eventual outage.
solution: This regular expression has been replaced with a substring function.

issue: Multiple Customers Impacted due to Upstream ISP.
root_cause: Multiple customers hosted in the Atlanta datacenter may be facing a service degradation due to an issue with one of the upstream internet providers.
solution: Connection has been successfully failed over to the second upstream provider, and all services have been restored.

issue: We are deeply sorry for the outage and especially all the trouble the aftermath has caused our users.
root_cause: A configuration issue (automated age-based Google Compute Engine VM image cleanup job) caused stable base VM images to be deleted.
solution: To avoid running out of space, we have an automated cleanup service in place to delete images that have been removed from our internal image catalog service. In addition, our cleanup service had been briefly disabled to troubleshooting a potential race condition.

issue: Stack Exchange Network Status — Outage Postmortem - Here we'll post updates on outages and maintenance windows for the Stack Exchange Network.
root_cause: The primary SQL-Server triggered a bugcheck on the SQL Server process, causing the Stack Exchange sites to go into read only mode, and eventually a complete outage.
solution: It took us 2 minutes to notice the issue, 5 minutes to locate the source of the issue and 10 minutes to get service restored. Approximately 3.5 seconds worth of data may have been lost as uncommitted transactions were rolled back.

issue: AWS S3 Connectivity Issues.
root_cause: We are experiencing some issues with some of our online services due to the ongoing issues with Amazon S3 services.
solution: We are monitoring the situation and will provide and update when services are restored.

issue: High latency spike and increased error rate. January 23 and 24 outage postmortem report Stream suffered two incidents of degraded performance in the past 24 hours.
root_cause: Both spikes were caused by a sudden increase of pressure to one of our PostgreSQL databases. Because Postgresql was slow at serving queries, HTTP requests started to pile up and eventually saturated the API workers' connection backlogs.
solution: The same operation was then restarted during low traffic hours.

issue: Checkout unavailable and springer.com partial outage. Additionally the journal and series pages on springer.com are also unavailable.
root_cause: Due to a network issue the checkout for springer.com, apress.com and palgrave.com is currently unavailable.
solution: Services have been restored, and we are monitoring the situation.

issue: Platform under heavy load.
root_cause: The previous outage was caused by issues with one of our infrastructure providers. While the platform was recovering, the attack caused extreme load on the servers.
solution: A DDoS attack was launched soon after we restarted operations.

issue: We have issues with our Solr Search Index. Please keep in mind that DOI registration or metadata updates are not affected by this Solr outage.
root_cause: Our Solr Search index is currently not indexing probably because of heavy database load. This affects the REST API, DataCite Search, OAI-PMH, content negotiation, and the Stats Portal.
solution: We have partially restored search functionality: the majority of DOis (9.5 million out of 13 million) are now available for searching via the REST API and DataCite Search.

issue: Issue Discovered - Service disruption in North America. During the incident, some clients may have experienced some brief interruptions or delays, including 503 errors, when attempting to access the xMatters web user interface.
root_cause: Their first priority was to mitigate any client impact, and then work to identify a root cause and build a solution.
solution: They confirmed that this had correctly mitigated the problem, and that all services had been restored.

issue: Users are unable to connect to Doppler servers. Our first critical outage occurred today, and it led to almost 2 hours of downtime but thankfully no data loss.
root_cause: We found a buried option in a submenu of the Managed Postgres Dashboard to force a rotation of our database credentials.
solution: After the primary database is in use, the old database is removed.

issue: Issue Discovered - Service disruption in Europe. The incident response teams quickly verified that notifications were not being sent and began working to isolate the cause of the performance degradation and to mitigate the impact to customers.
root_cause: The root cause of the issue was that unused or expired connections between services were not being cleared, causing a degradation in performance that triggered the alert from the xMatters monitoring tools.
solution: The teams began a rolling restart of the affected services to reduce the bottleneck in the queuing mechanism, which immediately improved performance and restored notification delivery service for all affected customers. When the rolling restarts had completed, the teams confirmed that all services had been restored.

issue: Issue Discovered - Service disruption in Notification Delivery.
root_cause: The issue was caused by an operator error during a clean-up process that reverted some services to a prior state, resulting in a misconfiguration between services.
solution: As soon as the resolution was applied, notifications began processing, and the teams continued to monitor the notification queues until the backlogs had cleared. Clients confirmed that they were receiving notifications promptly and that all services had been restored.

issue: Issue Discovered - Some users receiving User Interface errors.
root_cause: Clients were able to login but could not perform any actions or access any pages due to the error. While the issue prevented clients from being able to use the web user interface to send messages, view event status, or run reports, the system continued to process events as well as all notifications and user responses.
solution: As soon as the rollback was complete, clients reported that they could properly access the web user interface and that all services had been restored. The Engineering team completed the rebuild of the release artifacts and successfully redeployed the release later the same day.

issue: Issue Discovered - Service disruption. Other aspects of the web user interface were not affected, and the On-Demand service continued to accept all incoming events, send notifications, and process responses without interruption.
root_cause: This issue was caused by a software defect introduced in the 5.5.252 release of xMatters On-Demand, which included a change to the way that historical user roles were retrieved and displayed.
solution: As soon as the rollback was complete, clients confirmed that all services had been restored. The defect introduced in the release was repaired and the release redeployed via hotfix to all production instances later the same day.

issue: Issue Discovered - Service disruption in North America. at the xMatters monitoring systems alerted the Engineering teams to a service disruption with On-Demand services within the North American region.
root_cause: This issue was caused by excessive memory consumption by a monitoring service. The monitoring service was buffering metrics for reporting and consumed an excessive amount of memory, causing some database queries to fail.
solution: Once the promotion process was complete, clients confirmed that all services were restored and functioning as expected. Manual database failover performed - Monitoring service responsible is disabled - Client impact is mitigated.

issue: Gmail Add-on Delayed Storage of Messages. This related to a timeout inside our code that communicates with Gmail.
root_cause: This was due to a processing issue which we have now resolved._ We know a large number of our users have come to rely on our new Gmail Add- we’re extremely sorry it hasn’t been working to the usual high standard you would expect from a Capsule feature.
solution: Therefore we feel it’s only right to provide a more detailed explanation and assurances that we’re working to prevent this from happening again. Once we found this loop, we disabled the Gmail Add-on for that single user and restarted the process which consumes the event stream.

issue: Add-Ons Outage Post-Mortem Result - Mozilla Hacks - the Web developer blog Add-Ons Outage Post-Mortem Result By Eric Rescorla Posted on in Firefox Editor’s Note: July 12, pt – Updated Balrog update frequency and added some more background.
root_cause: Most Firefox add-ons stopped working around May 4th 2019 when a certificate expired. Firefox requires a valid certificate chain to prevent malware. About nine hours later, Mozilla pushed a privileged add-on that injected a valid certificate into Firefox's certificate store, creating a valid chain and unblocking add-ons. This disabled effectively all add-ons, about 15,000, and the resolution took approximately 15-21 hours for most users. Some user data was lost. Previously Mozilla posted about the technical details.
solution: Part of the reason for this misunderstanding was that in a previous incident we had disabled end-entity certificate checking, and this led to confusion about the status of intermediate certificate checking.

issue: North America Service Disruption - Notification Delivery. While the issue was being addressed, some users may have experienced delays when receiving SMS and voice notifications, or when injecting events for some integrations.
root_cause: This issue was caused when a backend queuing service stopped unexpectedly, resulting in a large backlog of events waiting to be processed which in turn prevented the services responsible for event processing from connecting to the queuing process.
solution: Once the backlog had cleared, the teams confirmed that all services had been restored. To prevent this issue from recurring, we have identified the following enhancements to the queuing process.

issue: Issue Discovered - Service disruption in North American Region - Multiple Services. Shortly afterwards, some customers reported that they were unable to reach their xMatters instances or were encountering a 503 error when attempting to log in to the xMatters web user interface.
root_cause: All services were restored, though the teams continued to investigate the root cause while manually clearing any remaining deadlocks.
solution: The automatic recovery process and redundant service architecture restored service quickly, and once the client's active event completed, system performance resumed normal levels. The incident in question was quickly mitigated by the redundant service architecture and automated recovery capabilities of the xMatters On-Demand service, and all services have been restored.

issue: Issue Discovered - Service disruption in North American Region – Integration Builder. Shortly afterwards, some customers reported that they were noticing delays in notification delivery.
root_cause: This incident was caused by an error within the cloud infrastructure-as-a-service provider hosting the xMatters On-Demand service.
solution: The teams confirmed that all services had been restored and continued to monitor the system while gathering further data around the incident.

issue: Unreliable or intermittent network connectivity for Linux and Windows builds. We are receiving reports of Linux and Windows builds where network connectivity is unreliable, intermittently working or slow.
root_cause: While this change was meant to improve maintainability, we are rolling it back due to the degraded network performance.
solution: The NAT gateway changes have been fully reverted. At this point, we've reverted half of the NAT gateway updates and a 50% of the Linux and Windows jobs currently processed have better network performance already.

issue: Network Connectivity Errors.
root_cause: We have received several reports of builds failing due to an unsuccessful TLS handshake to whereami.travis-ci.com:443 on one of our production servers.
solution: We have identified the production systems affected by this issue and have removed these from the pool.

issue: Issue Discovered - Service disruption in North American Region – Integration Platform. Some customers may have seen integration logs showing a number of errors related to script failures, and some events may not have been properly processed, Why did it happen?
root_cause: This incident was caused by integration scripts containing code that was not fully compliant JavaScript. During regularly scheduled maintenance on the morning of September 9, xMatters released a new version of the Integration Builder service to enable a faster, more efficient scripting engine.
solution: Once the rollback was complete, the teams confirmed the issue was no longer occurring and that all services had been restored.

issue: Intermittent DNS Resolution Errors, some customers experienced intermittent failure connecting to Atlassian Cloud.
root_cause: The root cause was an increased DNS error rate from our infrastructure supplier.
solution: We have identified the root cause of the intermittent failure connecting to Atlassian Cloud for some cloud customers and have mitigated the problem.

issue: Service disruption in North American Region. Some users may have experienced intermittent access to the xMatters On-Demand web user interface, and a delay or rejection when injecting events into xMatters.
root_cause: This incident was caused by a single database within one of the database clusters consuming a disproportionate amount of resources.
solution: The recovery process and redundant service architecture restored services, and system performance resumed normal operations. To prevent this issue from reoccurring, the Engineering teams will be taking the following steps.

issue: Desktop Clients Service Performance Issue.
root_cause: Issue identified to be triggered by slowness in a specific DB node. The impact was found to affect limited set of desktop clients and MySite users which were not able to authorize their accounts.
solution: Incident was resolved by implementing a workaround. Engineering team has been engaged for further analysis and corrective actions to prevent this issue from happening again.

issue: Syncplicity DNS provider failure.
root_cause: The issue identified to be triggered by a DNSSEC malfunction. The impact was found to affect desktop application clients and MySite users who were not able to resolve Syncplicity service DNS names.
solution: The incident was resolved by implementing a workaround.

issue: Desktop Clients Service and Web Site Service Performance Issue.
root_cause: The issue identified to be triggered by slowness in a specific DataBase. The impact was found to affect desktop application clients and MySite users who were not able to authorize their accounts.
solution: The Incident was resolved by implementing a workaround. Engineering team has been engaged for further analysis and corrective actions to prevent this issue from happening again.

issue: The incident started when our production Kubernetes Pods started getting marked as unavailable.
root_cause: However, due to a routine DNS maintenance operation that had been completed earlier, our clusters were unable to successfully reach our registry resulting in Pods failing to start.
solution: It wasn’t until we restarted the process with the cached DNS records that we were able to successfully fetch container images, redeploy, and recover our services.

issue: DNS resolution failure. Today at Pacific we experienced our second outage in the last two weeks.
root_cause: One area we found that could use a little love is in showcasing of a retry event. If request hangs it can create a visible delay to the user.
solution: To prevent this in the future, we are moving our status page’s DNS to another provider and will use a new dedicated domain.

issue: Issue Discovered - Service disruption in North America Region – Web User Interface. During the incident, some customers reported not being able to access the xMatters user interface.
root_cause: These connectivity issues led to a failure of the xMatters API to reconnect with the database. This loss of connectivity to the analytics database had a cascading effect that impacted the querying of a small subset of customer databases and access to the xMatters web user interface.
solution: XMatters engineering restarted the API service as part of the investigation into the cause of the errors. The connectivity errors cleared without xMatters intervention after the load was removed from the impacted services.

issue: Crates.io failed to serve requests.
root_cause: On 2020-10-29, the crates.io application failed to serve requests due to a wrong configuration change.
solution: The team promptly noticed the fallout from the changed and rolled back the application to the previous version.

issue: Today's Outage Post Mortem Today's Outage Post Mortem Loading.
root_cause: A bad config (router rule) caused all of their edge routers to crash, taking down all of Cloudflare.
solution: We removed the rule and then called the network operations teams in the data centers where our routers were unresponsive to ask them to physically access the routers and perform a hard reboot. all of CloudFlare's services were restored.

issue: Cloudflare outage on Cloudflare outage on Loading.
root_cause: During a maintenance of their private backbone network, an engineer made a typo in the Atlanta datacenter network configuration, causing all traffic coming from America and Europe flowing to this only datacenter, crushing it.
solution: Once the outage was understood, the Atlanta router was disabled and traffic began flowing normally again.

issue: During this incident, the success rate for queries to our API periodically dipped as low as 75%, and the dashboard experience was as much as 80 times slower than normal.
root_cause: A partial switch misbehavior caused a cascading Byzantine failure which impacted the availability of the API and dashboard for six hours and 33 minutes.
solution: Had the switch failed fully, all traffic would have failed over to the peer switch, as the connected links would've simply gone down, and the ports would've dropped out of the forwarding LACP bundles. For one of the clusters, service was restored quickly.

issue: It was this CNAME lookup code that contained the bug that caused the outage.
root_cause: Backwards time flow from tracking the 27th leap second on 2016-12-31T23:59:60Z caused the weighted round-robin selection of DNS resolvers (RRDNS) to panic and fail on some CNAME lookups. Go's time.Now was incorrectly assumed to be monotonic; this injected negative values into calls to rand.Int63n, which panics in that case.
solution: The most affected machines were patched in 90 minutes and the fix was rolled out worldwide by 0645. Discuss on Twitter Discuss on Hacker News Discuss on Reddit DNS Post Mortem RRDNS Bugs Reliability Follow on Twitter John Graham-Cumming | @jgrahamc Cloudflare | Cloudflare Related Posts Today we mitigated 1.1.1.1 Cloudflare is protected from attacks by the Gatebot DDoS mitigation pipeline.

issue: False alerts and check-in backlog.
root_cause: The root cause has been tracked down to an timeout error during check-in processing that wasn't handled correctly and put the process into a bad state.
solution: We've restarted the affected service and confirmed that it's processing correctly.

issue: SAML SSO disabled on all workplaces.
root_cause: SAML SSO has been disabled on all workplaces due to a faulty migration script. We are currently in the process of recovering SAML and will update this incident accordingly.
solution: SAML SSO has been restored for all workplaces.

issue: API outage. Overview On the 20th of January 2021, our REST API suffered a partial outage for 38 minutes, with partial service resuming over the course of 6 minutes, resulting in total downtime of 44 minutes.
root_cause: This was due to the fact that test data was present in the prod environment but not on the development or staging environments. The migration failed to apply everywhere (because the app thought there was no migration to apply) but the exception was only thrown because there was data in the table in production.
solution: We manually corrected the migration and service was resumed.

issue: Indexing Delay. The ingestion of logs from clients was not interrupted and no data was lost.
root_cause: This happened because of several simultaneous changes to our infrastructure that didn’t account for the need for more resources, particularly on clusters with a relatively large number of shards relative to their overall storage capacity.
solution: How we fixed it: We restarted the portion of our service that processes newly submitted logs.

issue: This left us unable to provide hosted builds during the time of the outage.
root_cause: This incident was caused by a database migration to flip the order of an index to improve a query’s performance, resulting in a degraded state of availability for GitHub.com.
solution: Once the authentication service was restored, we were able to quickly process the backlog of requests and return to normal operation.

issue: Our internal engineering team is now prioritizing work that will help ensure reduced impact to customers should such underlying outages happen again.
root_cause: This incident was caused by failures in an underlying MySQL database, which caused some operations to time out for the GitHub Container registry service.
solution: After performing a failover to one of our database replicas, the affected systems were properly restored.

issue: Once the foreign key migration was successful, the internal engineering teams then worked to slowly remove token records stored in our cache layer that were considered invalid.
root_cause: This incident was caused when a foreign key for scoped tokens exceeded max INT32, which resulted in high failure rates for GitHub Actions and GitHub Pages.
solution: We mitigated this with a long-running schema migration to change the foreign key to INT64. After these cached records were removed, newly created API tokens were able to generate new records and API calls resumed working as expected.

issue: Delays while running CRM integrations.
root_cause: This sudden bump in call volumes was due to the fact that we on-boarded a large number of enterprise clients today but it was totally our fault to not bump up resources allocated for integrations.
solution: Our backlog was cleared and as and when the new calls/texts arrived they were pushed almost immediately.

issue: Issue Discovered - Service disruption in North American Region – Web User Interface. at approximately Pacific, the xMatters monitoring tools alerted Customer Support to an issue where the web user interface was unresponsive or exhibiting slow performance.
root_cause: This issue was caused by a single instance attempting to load approximately 140,000 user records into memory. This eventually increased memory usage to 100%, resulting in an unresponsive service.
solution: While the condition properly triggered an automated restart of the web user interface service, the service was unable to recover properly until the underlying issue could be mitigated. The team then manually cleared the cache and restarted the web user interface service, confirming that it had resumed normal operation.

issue: Sisense for Cloud Data Teams Database Connection Errors.
root_cause: Starting some Sisense for Cloud Data Teams customers database connections experienced connection errors due to a recent code change.
solution: For these users, a database admin will have to unblock the Sisense user before full functionality can be restored. Engineers rolled back the code are monitoring the connections.

issue: Tenat account creation fails. Official response from AWS support: We can confirm increased API latency and increased API error rates for the ACM APIs in the US-EAST-1 Region.
root_cause: Tenant account creation fails due to AWS ACM increased API latency and increased API error rates.
solution: AWS response: We have identified the limit issue and have mitigated it.

issue: JavaScript error prevents notice closing after user choice.
root_cause: It looks like the version 1.7 of this library has a bug because the current version 1.7.3 is not conflicting with our SDK.
solution: The previous version of the Web SDK was restored and deployed back to production on 2021/7/8.

issue: Database connections and PlanetScale dashboard outage.
root_cause: Database connections and the PlanetScale dashboard were unavailable due to a bug introduced in a deploy.
solution: We restored service by rolling back the change.

issue: Mumbai (asia-south1-a) cluster is unavailable.
root_cause: Root cause We determined that the root cause was a configuration error introduced during a deployment configuration upgrade.
solution: Corrective actions We identified an issue in our CI/CD process that resulted in the initial misconfiguration, which has been corrected.

issue: Controller downtime. Components impacted Controller Summary The controller was unavailable to service new authentication requests.
root_cause: Root cause Leading up to the start of the outage period, automated monitoring alerted us to spikes in memory usage.
solution: Corrective actions seeing the decrease in service availability, we reverted the change and simultaneously made additional hardware available to the cluster.

issue: Following ongoing maintenance of the Actions service, our service monitors detected a high error rate on workflow runs for new and in progress jobs, which affected the Actions service.
root_cause: After investigating whether this mitigation would address the incident, we were able to confidently confirm that the bad record was the root cause of the issue, and removing it would restore the Actions service with no unintended side effects.
solution: We immediately reverted recent Actions deployments and started to investigate the issue.

issue: Controller downtime. Components impacted Controller Summary The Controller was partially unavailable to service requests.
root_cause: Root cause Leading up to the start of the incident was a planned maintenance period. The maintenance change propagated a configuration change across our Relay clusters.
solution: At a hot fix was deployed to the health-check system and it was enabled once again.

issue: Elevated API error rate in Dublin.
root_cause: Traffic to our Dublin infrastructure experienced elevated error rate due to a AWS outage.
solution: The incident started error rate decreased the incident was resolved by We are still performing impact and root-cause analysis, a postmortem with more information will be posted here.

issue: Summary of AWS Direct Connect Event in the Tokyo (AP-NORTHEAST-1) Region. Engineers attempted several mitigations, such as resetting failed devices and slowly bringing them back into service, but the failures continued and the engineers were unable to maintain adequate healthy capacity to fully mitigate the customer impact.
root_cause: This was caused by the failure of a subset of network devices on one of the network layers along the network path from Direct Connect edge locations to the Datacenter network in the Tokyo Region, where customers’ Virtual Private Clouds (VPCs) reside.
solution: While these devices were not correctly forwarding traffic, they were not being removed from the network through the normal automated processes that monitor and remove failed network devices. Customers started reporting recovery to their applications by JST and by JST affected networking devices were restored to a stable operational state and the Direct Connect service returned to normal operations.

issue: Delay in Trace Processing.
root_cause: Due to a failed hardware node processing of traces is currently delayed for a few minutes. We expect this to be fixed by our hoster in a few minutes and will update you.
solution: However the hardware node has failed and needs to be restarted from a backup.

issue: Notarize application: degraded performance related to meeting starts and notary functionality. Notarize application is experiencing degraded performance and increased error rates in the functionality related to RON meeting starts and notary functionality.
root_cause: The engineering team found the root cause of today's meeting performance problems.
solution: We can confirm that short term capacity increase mitigated this issue fully today.

issue: Issue with Pay API. We take platform availability very seriously and are sorry for the impact this outage had on your users and service teams.
root_cause: On Friday 22 October 2021 for a 16 minute period between -BST, the Pay platform experienced severely degraded availability of our Public API due to the failure of a Redis node used to enforce rate-limiting.
solution: Service was restored by automated processes within 16 minutes. What we will do to prevent this happening again We will.

issue: Controller downtime. This failover process resulted in a partial outage of the Controller, which was partially available to service requests.
root_cause: Root cause A physical hardware failure occurred in a single node within one of our Eastern US Relay clusters.
solution: Connectors and Clients attached to this node automatically failed over to a new node.

issue: Frame service outage across multiple regions.
root_cause: The root cause was related to how some of our more recently updated backend services were affected by the US daylight savings time change. Note, that users already in sessions at the start of the incident were not affected by this issue.
solution: We have resolved the issue and users can now start new sessions again and admin access to the affected Frame Dashboard pages has been restored.

issue: Web App is Unreachable. Both conditions were necessary for the Web UI to become unavailable.
root_cause: What we are doing to prevent it from happening again: We expect both necessary conditions – the failure of the network management software and that the web service was running on a single node – to be resolved by an already planned migration of our entire service to a new cloud-based environment.
solution: Later, we restarted the unreachable node, which restored it to normal usage.

issue: Service provider networking outage. Components impacted Controller Relays Summary Twingate services were unavailable to service requests on November 16th.
root_cause: Root cause Google Cloud Platform (GCP) deployed a configuration change in their infrastructure that caused all requests to return 404 errors (GCP incident description).
solution: While traffic was being restored, systems indicated that Connectors did not automatically recover. For customers using our Managed Connectors, these were restarted.

issue: Issue Discovered - Service disruption in All Regions – Multiple Services. For the duration of the incident, users were unable to access the web user interface, incoming signals were not processing, and notifications were not being generated.
root_cause: From preliminary analysis, the root cause of the issue was a latent bug in a network configuration service which was triggered during routine system operation." See for the complete report from Google.
solution: The incident team remained engaged until Google resolved the incident to ensure that xMatters recovered smoothly once services were restored.

issue: Long response times & Delayed Log-in on Hydrow. Slow response times and delays on Hydrow have continued intermittently as Amazon Web Services continues their attempts to mitigate their outage.
root_cause: The Amazon Web Services outage has been clearly identified as the root cause of this issue. They are working to fully restore service but Hydrow response times remain slightly degraded.
solution: Amazon Web Services has mitigated the issue that was causing problems for Hydrow services.

issue: Government Platform Connectivity. Nutanix Government Cloud services are impacted by an internet connectivity outage in the AWS GovCloud GOV-WEST-1 region.
root_cause: Starting at ET we observed increased failures with logins on Frame, Beam, Flow Central, and Clusters in the GovCloud region.
solution: AWS reports internet connectivity to their US-GOV-WEST-1 region is restored. As of ET it appears connectivity is restored and all Nutanix Government Cloud services are back to normal.

issue: Admin console billing functionality is temporarily unavailable. At Chargebee confirmed that the outage was resolved in their system and the incident was closed.
root_cause: Root cause The Twingate admin console relies on Chargebee API access in order to load billing information specific to the particular customer account.
solution: The fix was deployed all customers were able to access the Twingate admin console with billing functionality disabled.

issue: Error rates in all Amazon S3 datacenters began to quickly climb and our alarms went off.
root_cause: Message corruption caused the distributed server state function to overwhelm resources on the S3 request processing fleet.
solution: All server-to-server communication was stopped, request processing components shut down, and the system's state cleared. we'd restored internal communication between all Amazon S3 servers and began reactivating request processing components concurrently in both the US and EU.

issue: The diligent response efforts, including enhanced detection, comprehensive mitigation, and detailed investigation effectively disrupted the threat actor’s established infrastructure and eliminated their ability to continue their unauthorized access.
root_cause: Private tokens were leaked, and allowed attackers to retrieve data, both in internal databases, in private repositories and from customers accounts.
solution: Within three hours, we took action and disabled the identified compromised user’s OAuth token and GitHub account. Over the course of our investigation we implemented a production moratorium and disabled or rotated credentials of other critical accounts.

issue: WAF rejecting abnormally large number of requests.
root_cause: Between a, some API requests from authentic users were rejected by the WAF due to a configuration change.
solution: The changes were rolled back immediately and a fix has been implemented.

issue: Retrospective and Technical Details on the recent Firefox Outage - Mozilla Hacks - the Web developer blog Retrospective and Technical Details on the recent Firefox Outage By Christian Holler Posted on in Featured Article, Firefox, and Firefox OS On January 13th 2022, Firefox became unusable for close to two hours for users worldwide.
root_cause: On January 13th, 2022, a specific code path in Firefox's network stack triggered a problem in the HTTP/3 protocol implementation. This blocked network communication and made Firefox unresponsive, unable to load web content for nearly two hours.
solution: For those services hosted on Google Cloud Platform (GCP) these load balancers have settings related to the HTTP protocol they should advertise and one of these settings is HTTP/3 support with three states: “Enabled”, “Disabled” or “Automatic (default)”. This is why users who disabled Telemetry would see this problem resolved even though the problem is not related to Telemetry functionality itself and could have been triggered otherwise.

issue: Some logs submitted over syslog using custom ports are not being correctly formatted and are not available for Alerting, Searching, Timelines, Graphs, and Live Tail.
root_cause: Why it happened: We introduced a bug into our production environment, specifically in a new service called Syslog Forwarder.
solution: The lines displayed an error “Unidentifiable Syslog Source” and “Unsupported syslog format.” How we fixed it: We created a hot fix that corrected the bug.

issue: Crates.io unavailable. Ensuring builds with Cargo keep working is our highest priority, so we made some changes to the registry configuration to bypass the piece of infrastructure responsible for the outage.
root_cause: Due to an issue to our infrastructure provider, fully resolving the crates.io outage will take longer than expected, so we're executing our disaster recovery plan.
solution: We reverted the emergency change to the configuration of the registry index, and we're marking this incident as resolved.

issue: Streams UI spins waiting for git.
root_cause: Will I experience any Data Loss: You will not experience any data throughput issues You will not experience any data loss on any ingested data You will not experience any loss of data in logs (like audit, access etc.) You will lose monitoring data (metrics data that feeds the Stream dashboards like CPU Load, Events In/Out, Free memory etc.) due to the leader process restart.
solution: We have identified a system performance issue and have increased capacity in order to mitigate the timeouts.

issue: Consent notices not displaying for some users. Some more details on the timing: We correlated a deployment that took place around - with our monitoring and reports of customers experiencing issues that we started receiving.
root_cause: We have identified some notices not displaying consistently on Web and Mobile platforms starting 4pm due to the notice configuration not loading.
solution: The issue was due to rate limitations after cache was cleared and affected a limited number of users and websites/mobile apps.

issue: DNS resolution failures for managed databases. Yugabyte is aware of a of an outage impacting access to Yugabyte Managed databases.
root_cause: Because of caching behaviors in the global domain name system, customers did not immediately see an impact from this change. As those caches expired over time, customers began to experience failures when attempting to connect to their databases.
solution: Once it was traced back to a change in our domain registration, that change was reverted at approximately on 2022-04-20.

issue: Issue with Twingate. During the outage, both our private and public APIs were affected.
root_cause: Root cause After a detailed investigation, we found potential network glitches that caused connectivity issues and higher latency with different and unrelated parts of our system.
solution: Once the backend application pod restarted, the load balancer stopped returning 502 errors and things returned to normal.

issue: As CPU utilization on the database continued to rise, the Container registry began responding to requests with increased latency, followed by an internal server error for a percentage of requests.
root_cause: This increased CPU activity was due to a high volume of the “Put Manifest” command. The reason for the CPU utilization was that the throttling criteria configured at the API side for this command was too permissive, and a database query was found to be non-performant under that degree of scale.
solution: In order to limit impact we throttled the requests from all organizations/users and to restore normal operation, we had to reset our database state by restarting our front-end servers and then the database.

issue: While this did elevate error rates, it was not enough to cause a widespread outage and we should have likely statused yellow in this instance.
root_cause: Both instances that occurred were caused by the same contributing factors. In the first instance, an individual service team noticed higher than normal load and an increase in error rate on API requests and statused red.
solution: After follow-up that indicated the load pattern had subsided, our on-call team determined it was safe to report the situation was mitigated and began to investigate further.

issue: Log lines not ingested. During that time, newly submitted logs were never ingested and therefore not available for Alerting, Searching, Live Tail, Graphing, Timelines, and Archiving.
root_cause: Because of this versioning mismatch, logs from the ingester stopped being accepted by a downstream service (the “buzzsaw broker”).
solution: Why it happened: We manually reverted our ingester service to an older version (to solve a minor problem unrelated to this incident). During the procedure, the version of the container was reverted, but not the container’s configuration.

issue: Increased 502 responses to our Core API.
root_cause: We believe this is due to a recently introduced piece of code that is consuming more memory than it should be and are working on a fix.
solution: We have deployed a fix and are monitoring our container memory consumption.

issue: Slow and failing Agent chart data responses. Users with nightly versions of the Netdata Agent are experiencing slow responses between Cloud and Agent, resulting in failing or slow charts in their Cloud dashboards.
root_cause: In the mean time we've also found the true cause: the Agent was not properly processing incoming commands in the MQTT5 implementation, due to a bug in how the parser interacted with the buffer of incoming data.
solution: Reverting the default away from MQTT5 removed the immediate issue, and most Agents on the nightlies are now on the latest (v1.35.0-104-nightly). Latest, corrected version is v1.35.0-104-nightly.

issue: Some customers' logs are not currently being processed.
root_cause: Why it happened: We inadvertently released code into production that contained a bug in the parser service. This bug was known to us and in the process of being fixed in our development environment, but was not yet ready for release to production.
solution: The log lines were successfully accepted by our ingestion service, but a downstream service – the parser – removed some of them. This included exclusion rules made by customers in the past and then disabled.

issue: Core API Outage (Flagsmith Timeout).
root_cause: Even though we handle 5XXs on Flagsmith, here we were getting timeouts, and we got stuck await Flagsmith.identify Flagsmith outage was due to one AWS Availability Zone in eu-west-2 going down due to thermal issues.
solution: We quickly patched all services removing flagsmith temporarily, we deployed it for all the above services around Service was partially restored but since we couldn't patch frontend SDKs we were only able to partially connect (it was resolving with 5XX half the time) Web-core was affected more severely than Web SDK, with a crash when a certain flag wasn't available.

issue: Issue Discovered - Service disruption in North American Region – Web User Interface. at approximately Pacific, some customers in North America reported an issue to xMatters Customer Support where they were unable to load User and Group Performance reports.
root_cause: The scale of the change required for that morning's Pole Position release led to the misconfiguration as the interaction between features was missed during the QA process.
solution: This allowed the web user interface to more easily complete its processing requirements and the backlog of requests quickly cleared. Customers confirmed that performance had returned to normal levels and service had been restored.

issue: Ingestion and web UI outage. Action was taken to restore the service in a degraded mode, which recovered the Lightstep UI.
root_cause: Summary Lightstep UI and Data Ingest experienced an outage triggered by a planned database change on July 21st.
solution: A subsequent roll back of the database change restored all systems and services. Incident resolved, status page updated to “mitigated and monitoring”.

issue: Web: Login non functional.
root_cause: Workers are behind in processing due to the outage and data is not ingested in real-time at the moment. We are rolling out a small configuration change to get a few services back up and running.
solution: We performed a fail-over to backup hardware and the service has been restored.

issue: This incident occurred in August but was left out of the August report because it did not result in a widespread outage.
root_cause: Several GitHub Actions customers experienced issues because of the degradation so we decided to include it retroactively. there was a sudden spike in traffic to GitHub Actions which resulted in a higher than usual write load on our services.
solution: We mitigated the issue by scaling up the impacted database while also allowing a higher number of concurrent connections to it.

issue: Issue with upstream provider affecting custom domains.
root_cause: Customers with custom domains are experiencing service outages due to an issue with an upstream provider.
solution: We are no longer seeing issues with custom domains and the upstream provider believes the problem has been completely mitigated.

issue: Messages Inappropriate Image Incident.
root_cause: The attack was a result of a coordinated attempt to guess individual user account passwords, sometimes known as a 'credential stuffing' attack.
solution: We completely disabled messaging, blocked the attacker, made sure the image was removed and no longer accessible, and proactively alerted impacted users as well as our wider community. Seesaw’s swift response to this attack included the following steps: - As we resolved the issue, we completely disabled our messaging feature to ensure no one else saw the inappropriate message.

issue: Twingate controller service impacted. Medium/Long-term Based on data collected in this incident, we have identified areas where we can improve the behavior of our client and connection applications to better handle similar situations and allow connectivity even under controller downtime.
root_cause: Root cause After detailed investigation, we identified two separate issues in the application layer that interacted with each other. First, a code bug caused the system to re-evaluate the permissions of all our users at the same time, causing a significant load that saturated the system.
solution: Continuing to investigate the issue, with software and data migration rolled back to a known state, we initiated the process to fall over to our standby cluster to fully rule out any infrastructure issues.

issue: Frontend Builds Not Completing. Summary: From ET on September 21st, 2022 to ET on September 22nd, 2022, Shogun Frontend’s site builder was unavailable.
root_cause: This was due to the underlying service that powers the site builder being unavailable for the duration of this incident.
solution: In parallel, Shogun’s Engineering team evaluated and planned alternative solutions if access was not restored in a timely fashion.

issue: We received an internal report stating that port forwarding was not working on the Codespaces web client and began investigating.
root_cause: We statused yellow due to the broad user impact we were observing. Upon investigation, we found that we missed a step in the secret rotation checklist a few hours earlier, which caused some downstream components to fail to pick up the new secret.
solution: At this moment, we considered the incident to be mitigated. Our understanding was that the system would pick up the new secret without intervention, but in reality this secret was picked up only if the process was restarted.

issue: Bolt Sandbox environments are unavailable.
root_cause: A code deployment on 29 SEP 2022 had a bug that resulted degraded performance in the Bolt sandbox environment.
solution: After detection this morning we reverted the code and the sandbox environment was fully operational as of.

issue: Downstream services that rely on webhooks to receive their events were unable to receive them, which resulted in service degradation.
root_cause: Webhooks experienced a significant backlog of events caused by a high volume of automated user activity causing a rapid series of create and delete operations.
solution: As a mitigation, we disabled the automated accounts that were causing this activity in order to give us time to find a longer term solution for such activity. Once the automated accounts were disabled, it brought the webhook deliveries back to normal and the backlog got mitigated.

issue: Intermittent build timeouts.
root_cause: We identified certain organisations which faced intermittent build failures PT.
solution: We have rolled back since then and issue is resolved now.

issue: SevenRooms planned maintenance. In order to achieve this, customers will experience a planned maintenance downtime at approximately that is expected to last for 30 minutes.
root_cause: Working hand-in-hand with the Google Cloud engineering team, the root cause was as resulting from faulty infrastructure deep within the Google Cloud managed database layer (not within the SevenRooms platform application itself), causing deadlock and timeouts for incoming file system requests that were routed to faulty zones.
solution: Our maintenance is complete and all functionality has been restored to SevenRooms.

issue: Delayed Email Sync. Below is an explanation of what happened and how we will prevent another such interruption from occurring.
root_cause: Root Cause and Resolution The root cause of this incident was a bug in a vendor’s software introduced during scheduled maintenance on 10/18/2022.
solution: 10/20: Email sync functionality is largely restored.

issue: During this incident, customers experienced high latency in receiving webhook deliveries, starting GitHub Actions workflow runs, and receiving status updates for in-progress runs.
root_cause: GitHub Actions listens to webhooks to trigger workflow runs, and while investigating we found that the run start delays were caused by a backup in the webhooks queue.
solution: We scaled out and accelerated processing of the webhooks queue as a mitigation. the webhooks queue was fully drained and we statused back to green.

issue: Some users cannot log into Close. Below is an explanation of what happened and how we will prevent another such interruption from occurring.
root_cause: Root Cause and Resolution One day before the downtime, we published a large change to the way we load our app in order to improve the app'sperformance for our customers.
solution: In order to resolve the issue, we reverted both changes to a previous working version, and we also took the following steps to ensure this type of issue won’t occur anymore: We compared file per file of each release in order to understand the bottom of the issue.

issue: Users are unable to log into cribl.cloud.
root_cause: Users are currently unable to log into cribl.cloud due to a disruption of Cribl Cloud authentication services.
solution: Authentication service has been restored for Cribl Cloud.

issue: Cloudflare incident on | Cloudflare Blog Skip to content Multiple Cloudflare services were unavailable for 37 minutes.
root_cause: A deployment tool bug caused the production environment to reference a staging build version, routing traffic to an unauthorized endpoint returning HTTP 401 errors, cascading failures across Workers KV, Pages, Access, and Turnstile.
solution: When access to KV was restored, some Waiting Room users would have experienced queuing as the service came back up.

issue: Service disruption at Turso (see incident report).
root_cause: Incorrectly configured DB backup identifiers led to data leaks for free tier customers, and the subsequent fix resulted in possible data loss.
solution: They are scaled back to one automatically upon receiving a network request.
