issue: Heroku sync integrations are failing.
root_cause: Root Cause Doppler syncs secrets to Heroku via a Heroku OAuth application.
solution: Once the integration is reconnected, Doppler will re-enable all associated syncs that have been disabled and perform a fresh sync.

issue: Background updates failing.
root_cause: Due to an upgrade earlier today, background updates started failing. Crates published since have not been added to the index yet but remain in the queue.
solution: We have reverted the change and restarted the workers.

issue: Technical Issue with dashboard availability. This forced us to make some changes on the backend to prevent any performance degradation while working without distributed filesystem at all.
root_cause: We opened a case with AWS, as we worked around the clock on a plan to make our system responsive again, without knowing that the root cause had started on Amazon side.
solution: We replaced the file system for another one with more aggressive settings.

issue: Intermittent delays loading Web UI and running searches. This led to slow searches and slow load times for any part of the Web UI that displays data about logs.
root_cause: Upon investigation, we found that it had not shut down cleanly and some files essential to a normal startup had not been written to disk.
solution: Pods were gradually moved to other nodes and restarted, so as to prevent any interruption in service. We made manual edits to the pod that had not restarted cleanly so it could start again.

issue: Issues connecting to calls.
root_cause: We were ultimately able to prove that the deadlocking behavior was caused by a low-level behavior change introduced in a point release of MySQL.
solution: We disabled binlog replication and restarted the database to try and reduce the overall load on the database. At (T+1 hour), engineers were working on a script that would terminate stuck queries when the database suddenly restarted itself.

issue: Based on learnings from this incident, we are evaluating expanding our regional redundancy and have started making architectural changes to better handle temporary regional and datacenter outages, including more regularly exercising our failover capabilities.
root_cause: On February 7 our monitors detected failures creating, starting, and connecting to GitHub Codespaces in the Southeast Asia region, caused by a datacenter outage of our cloud provider.
solution: Codespaces in that region recovered automatically when the datacenter recovered, allowing existing codespaces in the region to be restarted.

issue: Invalid Role Lockout. Synopsis Customer was unable to login and received "unable to process callback" error.
root_cause: A bug discovered in Teleport 11.3.2 was the result of new validation that prevented login when invalid namespaces were used in role templates.
solution: Customer’s tenant was rolled back to 11.2.1, the faulty role was corrected, and the tenant was upgraded again to 11.3.2.

issue: Relay2 (us-east4) and Relay4 (eu-west6) Issue.
root_cause: On further investigation, we determined that an error in our Terraform configuration affecting network firewall rules had caused the issue.
solution: We disabled pods in the two affected clusters, which caused connected Clients and Connectors to re-connect to the next closest Relay cluster. At we corrected the error and redeployed the affected clusters, which resolved the issue.

issue: All MySQL servers on this problematic node experienced connection delays and slow query execution, leading to the high failure rate.
root_cause: We determined the root cause to be an unhealthy disk on a VM node hosting our database, which caused significant performance degradation at the OS level.
solution: We mitigated this with a failover of the database.

issue: Web App Outage - Permission issues on Kube cluster. We are currently experiencing an outage that is affecting our web app.
root_cause: It appears to be caused by a permission issue in our Kubernetes cluster.
solution: We have deployed a fix and are monitoring the issue.

issue: Some workspaces stuck in pulling image.
root_cause: We're continuing to identify the root cause of the EU workspace cluster Image Pull degradation.
solution: Already running workspaces will continue to run in the US, until they are restarted, at which point the nearest geographical region will be used.

issue: On March 15 our monitors detected increased latency for requests to Container, NPM, Nuget, RubyGems package registries.
root_cause: This was caused by an operation on the primary database host that was performed as part of routine maintenance.
solution: During the maintenance, a slow running query that was not properly drained blocked all database resources. We remediated this issue by killing the slow running query and restarting the database.

issue: Intermittent 404s downloading Node.js.
root_cause: The origin server for nodejs.org was being overloaded, and due to a recent configuration change, was now erroneously returning 404 responses for valid files when it was overloaded and couldn't read them from its disk.
solution: The Incident Starting on March 15th and going through to March 17th (with much of the issue being mitigated on the 16th), users were receiving intermittent 404 responses when trying to download Node.js from nodejs.org, or even accessing parts of the website. A build script bug caused by the recent migration of the website to Next.js resulted in the site being rebuilt and the entire Cloudflare cache being purged every five minutes, sending an abnormally high number of requests to the origin server and putting it under excessive load.

issue: Capsule is unavailable or slow. We're very sorry if you suffered from the periods of slow responses and elevated error rates with Capsule yesterday.
root_cause: We’ve tracked the issue down the a bug in our data stores query optimiser that resulted in what should have been a fast responding query taking several minutes to complete.
solution: While we fully understand the exact nature of the optimiser bug we have applied a fix that stops the bug from occurring.

issue: On March 29 users began to see a degraded experience with GitHub Actions with their workflows not progressing.
root_cause: We determined the cause of the impact to be a degraded database cluster. Contributing factors included a new load source from a background job querying that database cluster, maxed out database transaction pools, and underprovisioning of vtgate proxy instances that are responsible for query routing, load balancing, and sharding.
solution: The incident was mitigated through throttling of job processing and adding capacity, including overprovisioning to speed processing of the backlogged jobs.

issue: Connectivity Issues. This “large scale regional event” caused traffic from us-west-2 to move from Oregon Edge (HOI) to Seattle Edge locations (SEA4 and SEA19), which triggered AnyCast shifts between the two Seattle Edge locations resulting in connection timeouts for traffic originating from us-west-2.
root_cause: The root cause of this incident was a routing misconfiguration by AWS.
solution: This configuration change proved unsuccessful and the configurations were reverted.

issue: Increased delays on Jira Cloud and Jira Service Management Cloud integrations while creating/updating Opsgenie alerts in US region. The Incident caused degradation to customers hosted in the US region only.
root_cause: ROOT CAUSE The issue was caused by the sudden spike in the volume of messages, due to bulk actions.
solution: The incident was mitigated by scaling the integration component, which put Atlassian systems into a known good state.

issue: Delays in Android push notifications. REMEDIAL ACTIONS PLAN & NEXT STEPS We know that outages impact your productivity.
root_cause: ROOT CAUSE The issue was caused by an incident in a third party messaging service, which is responsible for delivering push notifications to Android devices.
solution: IMPACT The overall impact was - in Opsgenie_._ The incident only resulted in delays in Android push notifications only, and these notifications were delivered successfully after FCM service was restored and no data loss occurred.

issue: Issue Discovered - Service disruption in North American Region – Web User Interface. at approximately Pacific, some customers reported an issue to xMatters Customer Support where users were encountering errors when attempting to log in to the xMatters web interface.
root_cause: The issue was caused when a customer inadvertently initiated a denial-of-service attack by launching an excessive number of API requests.
solution: Once the traffic was mitigated, impacted systems were able to recover and customers were migrated back to their original data centers.

issue: Elevated rate of latency in India Point of Presence.
root_cause: Problem Description, Impact, and Resolution we observed increased latency for Publish API calls to our Mumbai Point of Presence.
solution: We scaled up capacity, and the issue was resolved.

issue: The Web UI is not accessible. This made the Mongo database unavailable to other services.
root_cause: The WebUI relies entirely on Mongo for account information and therefore became unresponsive, returning an error of “failure to get a peer from the ring-balancer.” While the immediate reason for the incident is clear, the root cause is still unknown.
solution: How we fixed it: We removed the WebUI from the service mesh.

issue: Events and Actions Outage in US East PoP. Events are not Being Dispatched.
root_cause: Problem Description, Impact, and Resolution On Tuesday we observed that Events and Actions messages were not being processed on our US PoP or EU Central PoP.
solution: Shortly after observing the issue, we redeployed a processing schema, and the issue was resolved.

issue: AWS degradation causing email failure. AWS is experiencing degradation which is causing our emails to fail.
root_cause: Our queuing system is currently processing backed up events, including webhooks, however because of throttling from AWS on the backed out events, there could be delays in processing the events.
solution: The AWS Lambda issue has been resolved, although it is throttled.

issue: Some Services Across US East Are Suffering From Partial Outage.
root_cause: During this time, we identified the root cause of the issue was due to a third-party service incident.
solution: In response, we redirected authorization services from US East to US West, and the issue was mitigated Tuesday June 13th, 2023.

issue: Increased error rate in Sandbox.
root_cause: We are seeing increased error rates in sandbox due to a provider outage.
solution: The provider has restored functionality and sandbox is behaving as expected.

issue: Partial service failure due to non-volatile Redis saturation. However, the utilization of our non-volatile Redis, which usually hovers below 5%, slowly started to increase.
root_cause: Earlier today, we deployed a bug that exposed a legacy system to excessive traffic, overwhelming our core Redis instance and causing cascading failures in certain functionality.
solution: Engineering quickly identified the issue and cleared excess data from Redis, restoring service. May 29th, - Fix deployed to remove the tracking bug We deployed a fix to remove the tracking bug.

issue: Increased error rate and timeouts.
root_cause: From around PT to PT the Routable application saw increased error rates and timeouts for requests in the web application and API due to a database issue.
solution: Operators restored database functionality and services recovered. At this time all functionality has been restored.

issue: We are currently encountering difficulties with our task processing system. Any changes that were not processed at the time were also re-run to ensure that the state was consistent with the expected changes that had been made in the database.
root_cause: We investigated multiple avenues to determine the cause of the issues but there were multiple ‘symptoms’ that made determining the root cause very difficult. One specific issue, which turned out to be a red herring, related to the functionality to forward core API requests to the Edge API.
solution: Once it was determined to be safe to do so, these tasks were removed from the queue.

issue: Elevated Error Rate. Below is an explanation of what happened and how we will prevent another such interruption from occurring.
root_cause: Root Cause and Resolution This incident began when our internal metrics service became degraded. Our internal metrics service is used by our compute platform to automatically determine the appropriate amount of resources needed to run the Close application.
solution: When the internal metrics service was restored at our compute platform provisioned the correct amount of resources and performance returned to normal.

issue: Problem with links in Notarize emails.
root_cause: We identified the problem with our third party email link wrapping provider.
solution: We believe we mitigated the biggest impact by making earlier changes, and resending specific emails as needed.

issue: Elevated Error Rate. Below is an explanation of what happened and how we will prevent another such interruption from occurring.
root_cause: Root Cause and Resolution This incident began after a routine deployment of changes to the Close backend.
solution: This query to the metrics service has been corrected.

issue: Problems logging into Spacelift accounts.
root_cause: The issue was caused by a change to our session authorization that was deployed to production.
solution: We have reverted the change and have verified that the problem appears to be resolved.

issue: Limit function not working for bulk actions. Below is an explanation of what happened and how we will prevent another such interruption from occurring.
root_cause: Root Cause and Resolution A bug was introduced in our API that caused the “limit” parameter to be discarded when bulk actions were being performed.
solution: We have increased the number of test cases covering this functionality to prevent similar issues from happening again.

issue: During this incident, customers experienced webhooks delays as long as 4.5 hours.
root_cause: We determined that the delays were caused by a significant and sustained spike in webhook deliveries. This caused a backup of our webhooks deliveries queue.
solution: We mitigated the issue by blocking events from sources of the increased load, which allowed the system to gradually recover as we processed the backlog of events.

issue: Twingate Service Incident -. The team quickly identified that our backend was seeing excessive timeouts from a 3rd-party API, preventing it from being able to process other requests such as authentication.
root_cause: Root cause The Twingate backend was exhausted due to timeouts from a 3rd-party API.
solution: After some initial fixes were unsuccessful, Twingate contacted the 3rd party and also disabled support for real-time updates that make use of these specific 3rd-party API calls. The vendor later confirmed and fixed the issue, and Twingate re-enabled the real-time update feature shortly after on the same day, August.

issue: Files Uploading is not working.
root_cause: To a Thinkific site, and challenges with viewing certificates was due to an open issue with a vendor.
solution: At this time, the vendor has implemented a fix that should see the ability to complete file uploads, and view certificates be restored.

issue: Multiple product logins. SUMMARY some customers were unable to login to Atlassian's Cloud products using id.atlassian.com.
root_cause: ROOT CAUSE Multiple Set-Cookie headers were unintentionally modified so that only the last Set-Cookie header remained in the response to user's browsers.
solution: Users with existing sessions were not impacted, traffic was incrementally restored to a previous build, mitigating the impact for users. We are prioritizing the following improvement actions to avoid repeating this type of incident: Automated tests to be put in place to validate that cookies are not being removed from responses.

issue: Identity integrations are not being triggered.
root_cause: Unfortunately, during the release to production, due to the high throughput on a particular table that it needed to acquire a temporary lock this caused a backlog of blocked connections waiting on the migration to complete.
solution: Once the restart was complete, the connections were restored and service was resumed.

issue: Atlassian Account login issues. SUMMARY 03: 30 PM, some Atlassian users were unable to sign in to their accounts and use multiple Atlassian cloud products.
root_cause: The event was triggered by a misconfiguration of rate limits in an internal service which caused a cascading failure in sign-in and signup-related APIs.
solution: The incident was mitigated 03: 30 PM by the rollback of a feature and additional scaling of services which put Atlassian systems into a known good state.

issue: Background Processing Delayed. Below is an explanation of what happened and how we will prevent another such interruption from occurring.
root_cause: Root Cause and Resolution a new version of the Close Application was deployed to production.
solution: To prevent similar issues from happening in the future, Close Engineering will upgrade our background task processing system to better isolate workloads that could potentially break.

issue: On September 19 while migrating the primary datastore for GitHub Projects, an incident occurred that disrupted 95% of GitHub Projects data availability for 3.5 hours.
root_cause: A misconfigured index constraint on the primary GitHub Projects database table caused GitHub Projects to become fully unavailable.
solution: We restored GitHub Projects data to its state from the beginning of the incident. New project data created by users while the incident was being mitigated was fully recovered and available to users.

issue: Archived reports cannot be restored for Plans that allow unlimited reporting.
root_cause: It is still possible to use the API provided to manually restore any reports until the root cause of the issue is determined and a fix implemented.
solution: The issue experienced by some customers has been addressed and functionality has been restored.

issue: Timeout and Loading Issue. We are marking this issue as resolved since incoming data shows services are recovered, error rates have dropped, and loading times are stabilized.
root_cause: We should start seeing more services gradually become healthy in time, and the loading speed will continue to increase, however due to the increased load times we are still considering this a partial outage. We are currently investigating an issue impacting our database which is preventing Chili Piper assets from loading.
solution: Services have been restored, and several sub-services were restarted in order to further support the recovery of all instances. Databases instances are being restarted to help mitigate the issue.

issue: On October 25 through 26, GitHub Copilot experienced multiple short and partial outages which affected code completions.
root_cause: These outages were due to the nodes hosting the completion model being upgraded by an automated process, and a subset of GitHub Copilot users experienced completion errors during this timeframe.
solution: In order to prevent similar outages from happening in the future, we have taken steps to disable the automated upgrade behavior that we identified as the root cause, as well as prioritizing improvements to our global load balancing during regional outages.

issue: General Service Unavailability. Circle is online, we are going to be deploying occasional updates that may require restarts or disruptions.
root_cause: Some shards have disconnected while we deploy an update We have implemented several fixes to address the root cause of this problem, as well as made it easier for systems to fail over in the event that problems appear again.
solution: 75% of the bot is reconnecting, we are monitoring it and investigating what caused the network drop Everything has been re-enabled and Circle should be operating normally. We have temporarily disabled new logins on the website while we troubleshoot some problems Circle is once again online.

issue: Issue with SSL certificates.
root_cause: This was due to a misconfiguration in the new CI for releasing our helm charts that used the internal Nginx ingress values files for the external Nginx ingress.
solution: Summary On Thursday Nov 9th the default certificate for the external Nginx ingress was replaced with a dummy certificate.

issue: Delay in Logplex processing.
root_cause: We discovered this morning that our Logplex pipeline, which handles Heroku platform errors, had an interruption in processing, which caused platform errors not to be recorded.
solution: This has been corrected, the backlog is being processed, and additional monitoring has been added to avoid this issue in the future.

issue: Trello is unavailable. The incident caused service disruption to all Trello customers.
root_cause: ROOT CAUSE The issue was caused by a series of changes intended to standardize Trello’s approach to authorizing requests, but had the unintended side effect of modifying a database query from a targeted operation to a broadcast operation.
solution: The incident was detected immediately by our automated monitoring systems and was mitigated by disabling the relevant code change.

issue: Database Connection Issues.
root_cause: Root cause The Twingate database connections exceeded the maximum allowed.
solution: We reverted the changes after which the increased connections receded and our connection counts returned to healthy counts.

issue: Cloudflare incident on | Cloudflare Blog Skip to content On Thursday, two independent events caused an increase in latency and error rates for Internet properties and Cloudflare services that lasted 114 minutes.
root_cause: A newly deployed DDoS mitigation rule exposed a latent bug in the rate-limiting system where flawed cookie validation logic caused HTTP request handler processes to enter infinite loops consuming 100% CPU, propagating across data centers.
solution: The new DDoS rule was disabled globally, and the incident was declared resolved after executing one more round of mass restarts and monitoring. By the Traffic team had written, tested, and deployed a fix.

issue: Control Plane Redis storage instability in us-east-1.
root_cause: This has been caused by a rolling of the storage nodes, the mitigation procedure is being identified and put in action.
solution: Functionality and normal redundancy is now restored.

issue: Increased Latency and Reduced Availability in the US, EU, and Global Region Groups. Between January 9th and January 13th, users in our US, EU, and Global Region Groups experienced multiple periods of increased latency and reduced availability.
root_cause: The issue was caused by a series of DDoS attacks that were targeted at a set of our customers, resulting in extreme waves of traffic to Fauna, each of which were many orders of magnitude above our baseline traffic patterns.
solution: After initial investigation, engineers realized that despite the fact that the requests were being throttled and sent a 429 response at the compute layer due to exceeding throughput limits, routing nodes were still experiencing resource starvation due to the number of connections being held and resources associated with request handling being kept in memory. Engineers identified and blocked offending accounts, causing the compute layer to short circuit the normal request handling process and return 410 responses for requests from those accounts, which shortened the time that each connection wa.

issue: On January 9, services in one of our three sites experienced elevated latency for connections.
root_cause: This was caused by an upgrade of hosts, which led to temporarily reduced capacity as the upgrade rolled through the fleet.
solution: We have increased that limit to prevent this from recurring.

issue: Some monitors are being auto-disabled. 2104 - Degradation to query service detected Our monitoring systems alert on a more significant spike in query error rates, which is acknowledged and escalated for incident investigation.
root_cause: Resolution and follow-up: Deployed fixes to prevent auto-disabling of monitors from query failures, addressed root cause that triggered query degradation and enhanced monitoring for such incidents; all affected customers were notified and monitors re-enabled.
solution: Incident and immediate action: Query service degradation was detected and resolved within the same evening; service restored by 2213. Investigation and secondary impact (Jan 26-30, 2024): Uncovered and fixed an issue where 84 organizations had monitors auto-disabled due to the service degradation.

issue: CSI Taxation Engine Outage. We have seen stable connections with CSI since their outage was resolved.
root_cause: For this reason we ask that any questions be directed to CSI until a root cause is provided. Once a root cause is provided to rev.io we may ask that you take precautionary actions if the root cause warrants such a response.

issue: Apigee Datastore issues (Cassandra) affecting API runtime traffic of Edge Cloud organizations in europe-west1 region.
root_cause: While we investigate the root cause, we'll continue to monitor this issue closely to ensure service stability. Some of the customers whose Edge Cloud organizations in europe-west1 region might be experiencing API traffic failures due to Datastore issues (Cassandra).
solution: The incident has been mitigated, and has been stable for the last 6 hours.

issue: JustCall app is loading slow. This issue resulted in degraded performance for some of our users, causing inconvenience and disruptions.
root_cause: Users were temporarily re-routed After a thorough investigation, the root cause of the API latency was identified as increased database response time.
solution: The API latency issue has been successfully resolved, and normal operations have been restored.

issue: Service returning 503s. Incident overview: A deployment of several database services inadvertently caused an overload of the supporting relational database, leading to a system-wide outage.
root_cause: Restoration of the service took around 60 minutes because of continuous thrashing in the database system.
solution: After service was restored, a small percentage of requests kept timing out due to an issue with our caching layer. Resolution and Follow-up: The deployment was rolled back, database and caching infrastructure was upgraded, and changes were made to reduce the load on the caching layer, fully restoring operational status.

issue: Australia data center vault login errors.
root_cause: A spike in API errors was detected by our team at due to an AWS ElastiCache error in the AU (Sydney) region.

solution: New trial cluster creation has been re-enabled in Belgium region.

issue: Trello is slow or unavailable. 13, 2024, Trello experienced severely degraded performance appearing as a full or partial outage to Atlassian customers.

issue: Service Interruption: Webhooks Signature Generation Issue.

issue: SDM Partial Login Outage. A partial outage impacting logins to the SDM app occurred CDT.
root_cause: The interruption is due to an improperly migrated table in our db prior to a version change.
solution: A roll back was initiated and functionality should be restored.

issue: Monitors partially unavailable. During the incident, our team communicated the outage through the status page and resolved it.
root_cause: Some failures remain following monitor cache invalidation The cache invalidation job has a race condition that is causing some stale data to persist in the system, although failed jobs count is now down to 20%.
solution: Cache invalidation job is restarted with fixed race condition Invalidation job is run for a second time, we see steady reduction of failed monitor runs towards zero. Improved Cache Management: We will enhance our cache invalidation strategies to prevent similar issues when introducing model changes.

issue: Backups failing for cluster versions 8.4.8, 8.5.1 and 8.6.0-alpha1.
root_cause: Our engineering teams have identified a bug that prevents backups from being completed for the following cluster versions: 8.4.8, 8.5.1 and 8.6.0-alpha1.
solution: The teams are currently working on a fix and we will update as soon as the issue is mitigated.

issue: Application Loading Issue. Below is an explanation of what happened and how we will prevent another such interruption from occurring.
root_cause: Root Cause and Resolution As part of an ongoing effort to increase security of Close application, we shipped a change to how authentication is handled between the application and internal search clusters.
solution: We have reverted the change, and will be improving our testing setup to catch these issues during development, as well as deployment and monitoring systems to catch production issues earlier.

issue: Interaction Processing Degraded Performance. Hello all, There is an outage with an external vendor that our system utilizes that we are currently aware will impact the speed of interaction processing and access to data within most tabs on the dashboard.
root_cause: Thanks and Regards, Observe.AI Technical Support Team The root cause has been fixed and we are monitoring our interaction processing backlog as it continues to trend downward, back to normal.
solution: Hello all, We are back in a stable state as the backlog has now completely cleared. It should be cleared within the next couple of hours.

issue: Error responses across multiple Cloud products. Summary On June 3rd, Atlassian customers using multiple product(s) were unable to access their services.
root_cause: The event was triggered by a change to the infrastructure API Gateway, which is responsible for routing the traffic to the correct application backends.
solution: The incident was detected by the automated monitoring system within five minutes and mitigated by correcting a faulty release feature flag, which put Atlassian systems into a known good state.

issue: On June 5, the GitHub Issues service was degraded.
root_cause: A misconfiguration of the service backing these events prevented the data from being loaded. We determined the root cause to be a scheduled secret rotation that resulted in one of the configured services using old expired secrets.
solution: These events indicate when an issue was added to or removed from a project and when their status changed within a project.

issue: LastPass Account - Users are experiencing login issues and slowness. During the release of this new Chrome browser extension, engineers noticed an exponential increase in connections to the LastPass platform across all tiers, and a subsequent increase in error rates for various APIs.
root_cause: Root Cause Analysis (RCA) Summary: LastPass users experienced slow performance or were unable to login to LastPass to access their vault.
solution: Specifically, we completed the following: Temporarily disabled non-critical functions so that LastPass users could once again login and access their vaults while traffic stabilized.

issue: Push Notifications Latency in Multiple PoPs.
root_cause: Problem Description, Impact, and Resolution we observed increased latency for delivery of mobile push messages in our Frankfurt and US-East points of presence.
solution: In response, we increased the resources available to the services and redeployed the service.The issue was resolved.

issue: Service Disruption: Gradient-Core NY2. Paperspace NY2 network outage Postmortem Incident Summary On June 16th, a significant number of virtual machines in the NY2 region became unavailable and went into Read-Only (RO) mode, which affected network availability.
root_cause: Incident Details Root Cause The root cause of this unexpected service unavailability is related to a core switch failure in NY2 that caused a large number of machines to go into RO mode. Impact As a result of the failure of the core switch, there was a spike in traffic that adversely impacted network performance.
solution: By on the same day, network connectivity was restored to the affected virtual machines. The affected virtual machines were restored to Read-Write (RW) mode on June 17th.

issue: Elevated rendering errors. How were customers impacted?, customers may have experienced failures when requesting new renders.
root_cause: The incident was triggered by a significant increase in requests, which our automated systems did not properly handle.
solution: A fix was implemented and the issue was resolved.

issue: Session APIs, Webhooks and Recordings Failures.
root_cause: Root Cause: A change was rolled out on 11 June 2024 that improved the performance and reliability for session data processing for larger meetings.
solution: Resolution: On noticing this issue, we restarted internal services, after which all pending data was processed and APIs started responding correctly.

issue: Database Connection Issues.
root_cause: A change to our SQL proxy deployments that was targeting staging and development environments was pushed to production due to a misconfiguration, causing our SQL proxy instances to restart.
solution: Components impacted Management: Public API Management: Admin Console Summary Twingate’s SQL proxies restarted, causing a brief failure to a small percentage of calls made to our Public API (Terraform, Pulumi, k8s Operator, etc.) and to the Admin console.

issue: Incorrect Rate Limits Applied.
root_cause: Due to a misconfiguration, these rate limits were being applied o low of a level, which interrupted access to the software repository incorrectly, for some of our users.
solution: We deployed a fix and are monitoring closely.

issue: Advanced Billing Outage. The disruption was traced to a specific part of our infrastructure.
root_cause: On July 1, Maxio’s Advanced Billing module encountered a temporary issue due to an unexpected surge in load. This caused a small number of subscription renewals to fail.
solution: Upon identification, our team promptly resolved the issue, and full service has been restored.

issue: Degraded system availability in Zeebe 8.5.4 (Camunda 8.5+gen6).
root_cause: Our team has discovered a bug in Zeebe version 8.5.4, which could result in one broker becoming unavailable on restart, resulting in degraded system performance.
solution: The upgrade path to SaaS generation 8.5+gen6 was already disabled.

issue: Issue Discovered - Service disruption in North American Region - Multiple Services.
root_cause: This issue occurred due to a sudden spike in the number of resources required by our backend services. The resulting memory overload issue caused some request handlers to time out before they could properly process incoming alerts.
solution: As soon as the restart was completed, the system resumed processing alerts and all services were restored.

issue: On July 13, the GitHub Copilot service experienced degradation.
root_cause: We determined that the issue originated from a resource cleanup job executed by a partner service on July 13, which mistakenly targeted a resource group containing essential resources, leading to their removal.
solution: The job was stopped in time to preserve some resources, allowing GitHub to mitigate the impact while resources were being restored.

issue: Beginning on network issues within an upstream provider led to degraded experiences across Actions, Copilot, and GitHub Pages services.
root_cause: This was caused by an unreachable backend resource in the central US region. This resource is configured for geo-replication, but the replication configuration prevented resiliency when one region was unavailable.
solution: Updating the replication configuration mitigated the impact by allowing successful requests while one region was unavailable.

issue: Service Interruption: Video Calls unavailable for a subset of customers. This resulted in a 55-minute service disruption for some of our customers.
root_cause: Root Cause: The incident was caused by an unintended removal of necessary permissions in our cluster configuration during a routine maintenance operation.
solution: Resolution: Our team quickly identified the issue and restored the required permissions, allowing the affected services to recover fully. We're updating our documentation and training to prevent similar oversights.

issue: EU Degraded State - Partial Outage. As a result, some of our customers were experiencing timeout errors (HTTP status 504) returned by Frontegg.
root_cause: Cause Analysis: The primary cause of the incident was the deployment of a new OTEL instrumentation in the API Gateway, which led to a significant increase in trace data volume.
solution: After identifying the problem with the OTEL propagator and collector, we increased the allocated resources and reverted to the latest working version. Resolution: Restarted the API Gateway to clear hanging requests and stabilize the OTEL Gateway.

issue: Beacon configs failing to load.
root_cause: Root Cause A database change that was intended to only be applied in our development environment for testing purposes was inadvertently applied to the production database, which resulted in the creation of new, empty tables for storing Beacon configurations and authorization information.
solution: The database change was rolled back, which allowed the Platform to once again successfully return Beacon configurations, which had persisted in the previously-used table throughout the duration of the incident. No configuration data was lost, and Signals Beacon functionality has been fully restored.

issue: Service instability and outage.
root_cause: A package upgrade was necessary due to a vulnerability, requiring additional updates to other packages. During deployment, some services did not restart appropriately due to a usage change in a newer container version, which requires a restart after upgrades.
solution: This was the root cause: the container service was not restarted, and all containers were stopped.

issue: QM platform not accessible.
root_cause: The root cause of this behavior is still under investigation and further information will be provided when it becomes available.
solution: Currently access to the QM UI has been fully restored.

issue: Automations and Background Actions Delayed. Impact: During the incident, a subset of customers experienced delayed background actions, such as rules, email notifications, imports, and exports.
root_cause: On 2024-07-26, a deployment of new code introduced a bug which caused delays for automations and background actions for a subset of our customers.
solution: We reverted this deployment, which allowed our system to catch up.

issue: Azure Service Degradation - affecting Flipdish Services.
root_cause: Azure Service Degradation - Investigation Underway We are experiencing performance degradation across our services due to an ongoing issue with our cloud provider, Microsoft Azure.
solution: Microsoft Azure services have been fully restored, and all Flipdish services are operating normally.

issue: Service Interruption: Video Calls unavailable for a subset of customers. Impact: Existing calls abruptly ended, and new calls would not have started due to this interruption.
root_cause: Root Cause: A change was rolled out to how we manage scaling for our media nodes, which had a bug in allocating new calls to nodes.
solution: Resolution: We rolled back the change and stabilised the system by temporarily provisioning additional nodes.

issue: Delay in Processing Identity Verification Transactions (US).
root_cause: From Jumio end, we don't see any error in our verification flow caused by AWS and we are monitoring the status and continue to work on reprocessing the pending scans.
solution: After careful monitoring, we are pleased to inform you that the recent instability on our US datacenter has been resolved, and all our services are now fully restored. Jumio's services have been restored to proper functionality and are fully available, but we have them under monitoring and continue to work on reprocessing the pending scans.

issue: Application and API errors. As a result, Asana became unavailable to users in all regions.
root_cause: At this point the application was fully operational, but asynchronous workloads such as automations and notifications were delayed due to the work enqueued while traffic was throttled.
solution: In response, Asana engineers throttled traffic for automations, webhooks, and API, and were able to restore primary functionality of the Asana application. The application continued to run with sporadic unavailability, when the underlying cause of the increased connections was determined and disabled.

issue: Service Interruption: Recording Start failures.
root_cause: Root Cause: The failure occurred due to an incorrect configuration setting during the update process, leading to subsequent attempts to revert to previous settings failing as well.
solution: Eventually, the setting was reverted to the original allocation, which took effect successfully. Resolution: The setting was successfully reverted to the original configuration, and the change took effect.

issue: CDN Sync Delays for Anaconda.org.
root_cause: In the other process, this is a new issue and the root cause is being investigated.
solution: We will continue to analyze the root cause for the incident and improve our monitoring for this kind of error We've restarted some processes which perform the channel synchronization.

issue: Unable to connect to Bitbucket Cloud via SSH. SUMMARY some Atlassian customers experienced an issue preventing users from connecting to Bitbucket Cloud via SSH.
root_cause: ROOT CAUSE A change to IP allow list evaluation was incompatible with a new Bitbucket Cloud networking configuration.
solution: REMEDIAL ACTIONS PLAN & NEXT STEPS To restore the SSH service, the team quickly rolled back the release responsible for the IP allow list issue.

issue: Application Loading Issue. Below is an explanation of what happened and how we will prevent another such interruption from occurring.
root_cause: Root Cause and Resolution At 1900 on components of our back end MongoDB database in one of our data centers came under anomalous load and became unresponsive.
solution: The database was restored to normal operation by 2000 without data loss. Once the affected components were identified and restarted performance of the Close app and API returned to normal.

issue: Recommendations and debug tool are not working as expected.
root_cause: Issues was caused by a sudden increase of traffic and complex usage from a 3rd party that cause strain the platform resources.
solution: The issue was resolved by 3rd party and we took also action to mitigate by temporarily adding resources ensure smooth operations on the platform.

issue: GitHub Actions and GitHub Pages services were degraded.
root_cause: We determined the root cause to be a misconfiguration in the service that manages runner connections that led to CPU throttling and performance degradation in that service.
solution: We mitigated the incident by diverting runner connections away from the misconfigured nodes, starting.

issue: Partial failure in joining meetings in US (West) and London Regions.
root_cause: Postmortem: VPN Tunnel Disruption Between AWS and GCP Incident Summary: we experienced a disruption in our media infrastructure due to a VPN tunnel outage between AWS and GCP. This outage affected communication between our AWS and GCP-hosted regions, causing media services on GCP to become non-functional.
solution: Resolution: The VPN connection was restored and services resumed the normal operation.

issue: A small number of instances are not accepting write queries.
root_cause: Whilst we monitor disk usage (to help prevent data corruption) we didn’t detect this issue as it was triggered by some backup-restore component containers running into an out of memory condition (2024-09-24 at ) resulting in being unable to serve disk metrics.
solution: A fix was released, tested in lower environments and rolled out to all affected instances (2024-09-24 at ) and then the whole service.

issue: Dark Web Monitoring - Possible Latency.
root_cause: Our engineers have identified an issue as being caused by an ongoing incident with one of our third-party service providers who are actively working towards a resolution.
solution: Our third-party service provider has corrected the issue and we are confirming that all services are functional.

issue: Webhook Service Degradation. Despite initial signs of system health, the disruption went undetected due to gaps in the system’s monitoring tools.
root_cause: Root Cause The issue was caused by a configuration change that resulted in the webhook delivery system not processing events correctly.
solution: Resolution Webhook processing was restarted, and we verified that all queued events were delivered without any data loss. The incident was fully resolved with all webhooks processed and delivered.

issue: System Errors in US-WEST-1 Region.
root_cause: During an upgrade to the region, the Operations team encountered an issue where a misconfiguration caused a service to falsely report as ready for operation.
solution: To address the situation, the Operations Team corrected the misconfiguration and restarted the affected service. the S3 service in the US-WEST-1 region was fully restored, and normal operations resumed.

issue: Elevated latency and errors for history service in us-east-1 region.
root_cause: The issue was triggered by an unexpectedly high volume of data requests processed through our shared infrastructure, overwhelming the shared history reader containers responsible for fetching this data from our storage nodes.
solution: Mitigation Steps and Recommended Future Preventative Measures To prevent this issue from recurring, we deployed dedicated infrastructure for high-volume data requests, and we implemented dynamic data bucket creation to distribute large data volumes more efficiently, reducing strain on our nodes.

issue: Billing Summary Page. a customer reported an issue with their Billing Summary page.
root_cause: The root cause of this issue was an engineering mistake when adding a new field to the database.
solution: The fix was deployed for all customers three hours later.

issue: Form submissions not triggering Concierge in legacy.
root_cause: Chili Piper experienced an incident as a result of a service migration that impacted the ability to load Chili Piper's Concierge snippet (marketing.js) in our classic UI / legacy product.
solution: The incident was resolved at approximately for all customers when the migration service was rolled back.

issue: Boards are demonstrating slow performance for Workspace Guests. We've identified the issue that caused the issue for slow performance for boards when loading them and opening cards for Workspace Guests, and we're now working on a fix for the problem and will provide a new update here soon.
root_cause: On October 15th, we identified that some boards were performing slowly for Workspace Guests.
solution: A fix has been released to all affected users, and the slow performance issue is fixed.

issue: Data feed issue with some Big Commerce customers.
root_cause: We identified the issue as being a change in the default delimiter for handing BigCommerce data feeds.
solution: We have corrected the issue and are re-indexing customer's who encountered the error, once the index is complete the problem should be resolved.

issue: Pipeline Web UI is Unresponsive. At times the database was entirely inaccessible or very slow to respond.
root_cause: There was no immediate customer impact, but we noted that backups of the database were unable to run successfully because of the increased load.
solution: We then deployed a new code change that removed all superfluous writes about metric usage to the postgres database.

issue: Fullstory APIs Unavailable. our API service experienced a disruption that resulted in a significant number of dropped requests and errors.
root_cause: Root Cause The root cause of the incident was a decrease in the capacity of our API service due to an unsuccessful deployment.
solution: We permanently scaled up the capacity of our API service to handle the increased traffic.

issue: Emergency Maintenance - Phoenix - Storage Controller Replacement.
root_cause: The root cause of the issue was found to be related to failed storage controller on a storage array, and we resolved it by replace the failed storage controller.
solution: With the replacement installed redundancy will be restored.

issue: General UI Slowness. Impact: Following changes made during recent scheduled maintenance, some customers experienced slower load times in the Codefresh SAAS platform UI.
root_cause: Root Cause: The traffic imbalance was due to a combination of technical configurations that resulted in uneven resource allocation across our zones immediately after the maintenance.
solution: These adjustments restored balanced performance, with monitoring systems ensuring stability.

issue: Increased scheduling delay across multiple regions. Impact: Our public API was partially unavailable.
root_cause: Root Cause: The issue stemmed from a database migration that inadvertently locked critical tables, impacting API and scheduling functionality.
solution: Database locks were removed, and check scheduling began to recover. Resolution: Once the database locks were removed, system recovery began immediately, with checks processing resuming across all regions.

issue: Platform instability. On PT, Hex customers experienced platform instability, including issues with kernel execution and site access.
root_cause: This disruption stemmed from an unintended effect of a recent database migration, which ultimately caused a backlog and impacted overall platform performance.
solution: Once the database stabilized, we rolled back the migration change, fully restoring service by PT.

issue: YugabyteDB Aeon cluster edits are failing.
root_cause: At we identified an issue with editing existing clusters in YugabyteDB Aeon, which is failing in certain scenarios.
solution: The issue has been mitigated, and a maintenance patch including an OS upgrade is available as a maintenance event. The Yugabyte team will monitor the progress, and once the maintenance event is complete, cluster edit operations will be re-enabled.

issue: Partial data capture issues (web & mobile). Postmortem 2024/11/13 Failed Tasks Not Retried / Pages Not Initialized On October 31st, 2024, an issue introduced in our service caused a small percentage (< 0.05%) of sessions to not process a portion of data within them.
root_cause: Root Cause Due to a code change that altered the behavior of an uncommon failure condition, part of our system marked the data in question to be “completed” when it had actually failed.
solution: Resolution After noticing some odd system behavior and finding that we had unprocessed data that should have been successful, we quickly traced it back to the code change, and deployed a fix immediately that would ensure no future data gets into this state.

issue: Elevated errors after deployment.
root_cause: We've deployed an update that caused elevated errors due to a caching error that didn't surface during testing.
solution: We've rolled back the update, implemented a fix, and rolled out the fixed update.

issue: The notifications service was degraded and stopped sending notifications to all our dotcom customers.
root_cause: This was due to a database host coming out of a regular maintenance process in read-only mode.
solution: We mitigated the incident by making the host writable again. To prevent similar incidents moving forward, we are working to improve our observability across database clusters to reduce our time to detection and improve our system resilience on startup.

issue: LastPass Support - Third Party Phone System Outage.
root_cause: Our Support phone line is temporarily unavailable due to a service malfunction with our third-party provider. The provider is actively working to resolve the issue.
solution: The provider has corrected the issue and they have confirmed that all services are functional.

issue: Increased Errors across Affirm Services. Affirm is still experiencing degraded service and high error rates.
root_cause: The root cause is related to excessive traffic on our backend database.
solution: The issue has been resolved and all services have been restored to full functionality.

issue: Order Fulfillment - Issue Detected.
root_cause: The incident was caused by a bad deployment of new set of rules in one of the critical internal services.
solution: The incident was quickly mitigated by reverting the change. To prevent this in future we have introduced more checks and process when making changes in critical flows.

issue: Unavailability of uploading from 3rd Party Services. Incident Summary the “Uploading from 3rd Party Services” feature of our platform was unavailable.
root_cause: Root Cause The outage was caused by a synchronization issue between repositories during a server configuration update.
solution: The incident was fully resolved, and service was restored. Resolution The application configuration was updated and service functionality was fully restored.

issue: Hasura Cloud AWS us-east-1: Increased error rates and latency. This surge caused elevated latency and error rates across projects in the region, with some projects experiencing up to 90% dropped traffic during peak periods.
root_cause: Third Spike ( - PT) 12.41M requests Peak of 30,000 requests/second at approximately Root Cause Our gateway clusters, which are shared across all projects in a region, were unable to scale quickly enough to handle the sudden flood of requests.
solution: Preventive Measures We are implementing the following improvements to prevent similar incidents.

issue: Elevated URL API Errors. Incident Summary On 26 November 2024, an issue with our URL API was identified, causing a partial outage of the service.
root_cause: Root Cause The issue was caused by a CDN configuration change that altered cache key behavior, significantly increasing traffic to our origin servers.
solution: The incident was fully resolved, and service was restored. Resolution The configuration change was identified as the root cause and rolled back.

issue: Network issues affecting all regions.
root_cause: The cause behind this service degradation was due to an error within the internal messaging queue service responsible for taking client requests and routing them to our global database cluster.
solution: Once this action was taken, which restored service, the teams then worked to correct the root cause by working to recover the internal messaging queue and resume the automated task of proper client request handling. The system has been restored to fully operational in all regions.

issue: System Down. All workloads were disrupted, leading to downtime for all clients in the Mumbai region.
root_cause: The root cause was the accidental deletion of a critical configuration, which disrupted communication between cluster nodes and the control plane, leading to a regional system-wide outage.
solution: Resolution Access was restored by recreating the deleted configuration.

issue: Intermittent Pipeline Service Degradation.
root_cause: What we are doing to prevent it from happening again: We discovered our Vector partitions are configured to use more CPU cores than necessary; under high load, the increased CPU usage causes pods to crash.
solution: This allowed the accounts on all other Vector partitions to function normally again; we restarted Pipeline processing on their pods and data began to flow to destinations again.

issue: Quality degradation for a small portion of rendered images in the EU. Timeframe December 9th, - December 10th, Impact A small percentage of image requests served by a single machine in the EU region experienced quality degradation.
root_cause: Root Cause A hardware failure on one of the rendering machines resulted in images with artifacts being delivered to users.
solution: Corrective Actions To prevent this issue from happening in the future, we will: Investigate and implement automated image quality testing for active rendering machines Replace and refresh machines on a more frequent basis to minimize impact of single machine failures Upgrade cache tooling for targeted issue resolution.

issue: GraphQL API partial outage.
root_cause: When the GraphQL API was deployed to release a performance improvement in model field selection, a regression was introduced for customers who only selected the content model from the model, which is a primary usecase of our Gatsby integration.
solution: The GraphQL API was rolled back to fix the issue.

issue: Errors and Latency Across All Services in our US-East and US-West Points of Presence. This issue occurred because a previously unseen pattern of customer behavior overwhelmed a cache in the PAM system, causing memory to become constrained and performance to degrade.
root_cause: Problem Description, Impact, and Resolution 2024-12-11 we observed increased latencies and error rates across all services in our US-East point-of-presence, a few minutes later, in US-West as well.
solution: We increased capacity and the issue was mitigated in both points-of-presence and declared resolved.

issue: New logs are not available for some accounts. Our service is also designed to retain submitted log lines, even if the indexing portion of our service cannot process them immediately; these log lines can be indexed later, when the service is functional again.
root_cause: This was due to a sudden increase in the volume of log lines sent to Mezmo by accounts that happened to be assigned to this pod.
solution: How we fixed it: We restarted the pod that had run out of disk space.

issue: Longer loading time of the UI.
root_cause: The EU data center experienced performance degradation due to a higher-than-usual operational load.
solution: We scaled up the data center to handle the additional operations efficiently.

issue: Users experienced intermittent errors and timeouts when accessing github.com.
root_cause: The errors were caused by our web servers being overloaded as a result of planned maintenance that unintentionally caused our live updates service to fail.
solution: We mitigated the incident by rolling back the changes from the planned maintenance and scaling up the service to handle the influx of traffic from WebSocket clients. We were able to assess the broad scope of the impact to our services only after the incident was mitigated.

issue: Incorrect MIME Type Headers for JavaScript SDK Plugin Artifacts. Some customers experienced the issue earlier as their regions picked up the changes, while others saw delayed or minimal impact.
root_cause: Impact: The issue did not affect all customers uniformly due to the nature of content distribution via the CDN.
solution: Resolution: The incorrect MIME type was promptly corrected to application/javascript, and normal functionality was restored.

issue: Reports of Superwall.com being Inaccessible. However, our data streaming vendor is still suffering an outage so we've been unable to collect data during this period.
root_cause: We've found the root cause of the issue and are working on mitigating and expecting a resolution from our critical vendor shortly.
solution: We've restored service so all the SDK and Dashboard endpoints and now operational.

issue: Account Summary API Issue.
root_cause: DriveWealth has addressed the root cause of the issues that impacted a subset of API endpoints.
solution: We anticipate that the issue will be resolved by early afternoon and will continue to provide updates as more information becomes available. The updated list of impacted APIs is as follows: Account Summary Redemptions Share Transfer Deposits DriveWealth has remediated the root cause for the issues that impacted the Account Summary API and Redemptions API.

issue: Event-Triggered Journeys Delays Ingesting New Users. The deployment resolved the issue, and error rates dropped significantly.
root_cause: The issue originated from errors in the workflow-entrance-trigger pods, causing a significant backlog in processing.
solution: This issue is now resolved and the backlog is completely drained. Actions Taken The workflow-entrance-trigger service was updated to the latest version, and additional pods were scaled up to process the backlog faster.

issue: Cloudflare outage on | Cloudflare Blog Skip to content Note: This post was updated to clarify the relationship of the internal WAF tool with the incident on Dec.
root_cause: A configuration change to disable an internal WAF testing tool propagated globally without a gradual rollout, triggering a Lua exception in the proxy's rulesets module that caused HTTP 500 errors for customers using the Cloudflare Managed Ruleset.
solution: The incident was resolved at (~25 minutes total impact), when all services were fully restored. The issue was identified shortly after the change was applied, and was reverted after which all traffic was served correctly.

issue: Cloudflare incident on | Cloudflare Blog Skip to content Multiple Cloudflare services, including our R2 object storage, were unavailable for 59 minutes on Thursday.
root_cause: Human error during abuse remediation inadvertently disabled the R2 Gateway service instead of a specific endpoint, due to insufficient validation safeguards in admin tooling.
solution: This impacted less than 0.049% of all cacheable requests served during the incident window.User-facing requests for assets to sites with Cache Reserve did not observe failures as cache misses failed over to the origin. Time Event 2025-02-06 The R2 Gateway service is inadvertently disabled while responding to an abuse report.

issue: We’re deeply sorry for this incident and the disruption it may have caused to you or your users.
root_cause: During credential rotation, the R2 engineering team accidentally deployed new storage credentials to the default environment instead of production by omitting the --env production flag, causing the R2 Gateway to fail authentication once old credentials were removed.
solution: Once the root cause was identified and we realized we hadn’t deployed the new credentials to the production R2 Gateway service, we deployed the updated credentials and service availability was restored. User-facing requests for assets to sites with Cache Reserve did not observe failures as cache misses failed over to the origin.

issue: The degradation in performance was limited to traffic between Cloudflare and AWS us-east-1.
root_cause: A single customer's traffic surge from AWS us-east-1 saturated Cloudflare's peering links; AWS's BGP prefix withdrawals to mitigate congestion paradoxically rerouted traffic to already-strained alternate paths, compounded by a pre-existing half-capacity link failure and insufficient DCI capacity.
solution: Through close collaboration, we successfully alleviated the congestion and fully restored services for all affected customers. That caused a long tail of latency that may have impacted some customers, which is why you see the packet drops resolve before the customer latencies are restored.

issue: Cloudflare service outage | Cloudflare Blog Skip to content Cloudflare suffered a significant service outage that affected a large set of our critical services, including Workers KV, WARP, Access, Gateway, Images, Stream, Workers AI, Turnstile and Challenges, AutoRAG, Zaraz, and parts of the Cloudflare Dashboard.
root_cause: Workers KV relies on a central data store for its source of truth; a failure of the third-party cloud provider backing that store caused a complete outage for cold reads and writes.
solution: Some providers may require a manual re-synchronization but most customers would have seen immediate service restoration once Access’ SCIM service was restored due to retry logic by the identity provider.Service authentication based logins (e.g. Workers KV removed a storage provider as we worked to re-architect KV’s backend, including migrating it to Cloudflare R2, to prevent data consistency issues (caused by the original data syncing architecture), and to improve support for data residency requirements.

issue: Service disruption at Razorpay (see incident report).
root_cause: A RDS hardware failure highlighted an incorrect MySQL configuration which resulted in major data loss in a financial system.
solution: The AWS tech-support informed us that since the master instance has gone through a multi-AZ failover, they had replaced the old master with a new machine, which is a routine. So, when the application failed over to the standby machine, it again entered a new row with auto-increment-id as X+1.

issue: Service Instability - (US). We are pleased to inform you that the 504 timeout error has been resolved, and our services in the U.S.
root_cause: The US services were unavailable from: 2025-01-01 Description: 2025-01-01, we discovered an instability in our US DC.
solution: After careful monitoring, we are pleased to inform you that the recent instability in our US datacenter has been resolved, and all our services are now fully restored.

issue: Intermittent delays in job updates of Activity page on Helios.
root_cause: We want to let our customers know that on Jan 2nd 2025 we identified delays in processing the data on the backend between 5 AM to 10 AM.

issue: Admin Center page is not reachable. starting at some users experienced issues loading the Admin Center page.

issue: Application UI Intermittently Inaccessible. Below is an explanation of what happened and how we will prevent another such interruption from occurring.

issue: Networking availability impact in AP-SOUTHEAST-2. issue: Vault login errors - resolved. our DevOps team was alerted to elevated API error rates in production.

root_cause: On 26 June 2025, we experienced system errors in our us-east-1 and us-east-2 regions due to an unplanned data center thermal event.

issue: Increased errors and latency in FRA region.
root_cause: The root cause discussed in this analysis was identified and corrected on Monday, June 30. Problem Description, Impact, and Resolution Recently, to ensure PubNub had access to more cloud server capacity across our many regions, we introduced new instance types to our system to provide a more heterogeneous set of instance types on which PubNub’s services run.
solution: The issue was mitigated once we identified this issue and configured the affected services to run on other instance types and launched more capacity.

issue: Users experiencing errors attempting to load Bitbucket. Incident Narrative a service disruption occurred leaving Atlassian customers unable to access Bitbucket.
root_cause: Root Cause The root cause of the incident was traced to a network ACL misconfiguration during a routine update.
solution: This network misconfiguration caused a service outage until the rule was corrected restoring normal service operations.

issue: API down. This resulted in connection starvation for new requests, resulting in timeouts and 5XX responses starting at 13:59Z.

issue: 503 Errors on File Upload. During this period, users may have noticed a temporary UI change and limited access to certain cloud upload options.

solution: The service began stabilizing after the mitigation, with full functionality restored shortly thereafter.

issue: Failed delivery of notification emails for very large query submissions and some forward-link alerts.

IF Submissions from Metadata Manager and the Simple Text Query form have been restored.

solution: You can read the provider’s incident report here, which outlines in detail what occurred and how they remediated the issue. Resolution Steps: Our third party provider mitigated the issue.

issue: Dashboard Login Failure - Identified. Dashboard Login Failure - Postmortem Summary: The system experienced a performance reduction that resulted in slower API response times and an unresponsive front-end dashboard.

issue: New uploads not transitioning to playable.

solution: How we responded We promptly identified the bug, rolled back the changes, and deployed a script to mark the affected videos as playable.

issue: Batch SaaS EU1 - Degraded performance. We’re currently experiencing degraded performance in our EU1 region.
root_cause: The root cause has been identified and our engineering teams have applied a fix. a subset of jobs posted to EU1 region were impacted due to this issue.
solution: The service has now been restored to normal operational status.

solution: As soon as these changes were completed, all requests were properly routed to the correct asset upload service, and normal functionality was restored.

issue: Cluster creation not available.
root_cause: Due to a problem with a dependent service, some features of our control plane are currently impacted. At this time, users may experience the following limitations.

issue: Activity Log fails to load or return errors for some users.

issue: Permission issues affecting repo.anaconda.com/pkgs.
root_cause: The incident was caused by a recent configuration change at which we reverted. The public repository at repo.anaconda.com/pkgs is returning errors, preventing installing packages.

issue: Incident affecting run scheduling.

solution: The backlog has cleared and the system appears to be operating correctly again.

issue: US Pipeline Export Delays.
root_cause: We identified a Data Pipeline export delay affecting US-based projects.
solution: While most tasks have been cleared, a few may require additional time.

issue: Elevated Presence Latency and Errors in FRA.
root_cause: The root cause of the memory condition was a caching system—operated by a third-party vendor—that we rely heavily on for this service began responding slowly at first, and later timing out.
solution: While nodes that run into critical issues are generally taken out of service and replaced automatically, this issue began affecting our system faster than new capacity could be brought online to mitigate the incident. We also changed the retry configuration to prevent this kind of retry storm from happening again.

issue: Monthly Payment Gateway payouts delayed. The outage has been resolved, and we will reschedule these payouts for later this week.

solution: Our team has reprocessed all delayed payouts and we've confirmed they have been delivered as expected.

issue: Cannot sign into 1Password accounts. Impact on Customers During the service disruption, some customers experienced degraded performance when accessing their 1Password vaults and signing in.
root_cause: Root Cause Analysis: The root cause was an error in the configuration of an attempted rollback.
solution: The issue was resolved by correcting the misconfiguration and restarting the web application servers, fully restoring service: Service is fully restored for all customers.

issue: Issue Discovered - Service disruption in North America – Multiple Services. Some xMatters customers may have experienced delays when receiving notifications or noticed failed alerts in the system.
root_cause: The issue occurred because of a network problem that disrupted communication between parts of the queuing system.
solution: As the system recovered, some performance was degraded until normal operation could be restored. The teams quickly mitigated the issue and restored performance by redirecting traffic from our message queuing system in the affected region (us-central) to our message queuing system in another local region (us-east).

issue: Chat messages may fail to deliver Prod 1. Summary customers experienced an incident where chat messages failed to deliver in one of our production environments.
root_cause: Root Cause A production issue impacted our chat messaging service, causing messages to not deliver. This was due to an unavailable container image, which prevented the service from recovering after an internal issue.
solution: The issue was resolved by identifying and using a previously stable image. The problem was resolved by reverting to a previous, stable image.

issue: Increased occurrence processing pipeline latency.
root_cause: The current pipeline delay is caused by an incident at our cloud provider which is resulting in higher rates of packet loss within the private network.
solution: All Rollbar systems are performing normally and all pipeline backlogs have cleared.

issue: US1 - Upload and Download failing requests. This led to a cascade of issues, including database locking, request timeouts, and connection pool exhaustion.
root_cause: Root Cause: The primary root cause was an exceptionally high volume of simultaneous uploads targeting the same objects, which triggered a bottleneck in the database due to transaction contention.
solution: Database transactions can cause issues because they hold locks on the affected data, preventing other operations from accessing or modifying that data until the transactions are committed or rolled back.

issue: Issue affecting several Tink products. This, in turn, caused degradation in the availability of our products.
root_cause: Root Cause Analysis After a thorough investigation, it was identified that there was an error in one of the third-party libraries used to read feature flags, which led to an unrecoverable runtime error in a critical service.
solution: Remediation Once the issue was identified, all affected instances were restarted.

issue: Users experienced inaccurate or incomplete results, failures to load certain pages (like issues, pull requests, projects, and deployments) and broken components (like actions workflow and label filters).
root_cause: The incident was triggered by intermittent connectivity issues between our load balancers and search hosts. While retry logic initially masked these problems, retry queues eventually overwhelmed the load balancers, causing failure.
solution: The query failures were mitigated at after throttling our search indexing pipeline to reduce load and stabilize retries.

issue: InsightVM - Remediation Projects/Goals & SLAs.
root_cause: Remediation Project updates have returned to normal, but ticketing integrations (e.g, Jira) are delayed due to a backlog.
solution: You will begin to see projects and goals update, but full processing capacity will be restored gradually.

issue: Intermittent Access Issues for Sisense APIs and Support Portal. Some customers experienced intermittent issues when accessing Sisense APIs and the Support Portal.
root_cause: The disruption was caused by a dynamic adjustment within our traffic bot management rules, which automatically adapt based on observed traffic patterns.
solution: Once the issue was identified, our security engineering team promptly reverted the adjustment, and services were quickly restored.

issue: Hubspot integration authorization issues.
root_cause: The root cause appears to be related to a permission scope that Hubspot used to provide "as requested" now requires explicit permissions for it to work.
solution: A fix was deployed and all connections to Hubspot are working again. We have deployed a fix which essentially removes the need for this scope.

issue: 2025-August-19 Resolved Service Incident.

solution: How we fixed it: The deployment was rolled back.

issue: Incorrect Liveness Rejections.

solution: Action Plan Our engineering team will review the affected service in detail and work on making it more robust to prevent similar issues in the future.

issue: Studio - Animations not rendering for accounts in the EU data centre.

issue: Reports of issues loading some Hosted Sites.
root_cause: Between –, fewer than 5% of Webflow-hosted sites experienced intermittent loading issues due to an upstream provider.

issue: Database instance write performance impacted. Specifically, an incorrect parameter setting in the data pipeline led to a bottleneck, which slowed down the processing speed.

issue: Batch SaaS EU1/US1 - Partial Outage.

solution: The issue was traced to a misconfiguration in one of our services, which has since been corrected, and normal performance has been restored.

issue: 403 ERROR PROD 1 & 2. During this window, some users were unable to log in; users already logged in were generally unaffected.
root_cause: Root Cause A security policy update inadvertently restricted access required for public web content.
solution: The update was then reverted and service was restored. Reverting the update restored normal behavior.

issue: Issues loading Rippling. Summary _All times are in the US Pacific timezone._ On Tuesday, Rippling experienced a major outage that left users unable to access the Rippling application.
root_cause: The outage was caused by two incompatible changes made in separate components of our system. Together, these changes triggered an infinite loop of database queries, overwhelming a critical database and dramatically increasing site latency.
solution: Below, we will explain in detail how the issue arose, how it bypassed our safety procedures, and the future steps we are taking to prevent similar issues from occurring. Engineers identified this secondary issue and disabled the rate-limiting, allowing the app to fully recover.

issue: Elevated API Errors: Some servers started consuming abnormally high memory, causing slow response times and high error rates.
root_cause: All servers completed restarts, and error rates returned to normal levels Root Cause Analysis: A poorly performing cache operation was triggered repeatedly in a short period of time across multiple servers, leading directly to greatly delayed responses.
solution: 92% of the impact was mitigated within 13 minutes at by automation scaling up infrastructure. Mitigation Steps: Automatic instance scaling restored over 98% of operational capacity after 13 minutes.

issue: Da Vinci - Proof Runner Down. Incident Summary On September 4th, 2025, some users were unable to see campaign proofs in the Proof tab after their campaigns had finished running.

Corrective actions To prevent this from happening again, Engineering is: Adjusting how system updates are applied so that changes for new services do not unintentionally impact existing ones.

issue: Increased Error Rate and Latency for Presence.
root_cause: Problem Description, Impact, and Resolution we observed increased error rates and latency for our Presence service in our San Jose, Virginia, and Tokyo regions.

issue: Multiple Deployments Admin Panel Login Failures. Moving forward, Duo is enhancing our testing processes to identify incompatibilities before implementing approved changes and to reduce downtime for our customers.

root_cause: This resulted in partial sync failures for that table because of a breach of the warehouse column limit, which prevented data from being fully written.

issue: Temporary Database Routing Issue. Impact: A subset of clients connecting through the eu-central-1 region experienced increased error rates and timeouts when accessing certain databases.

issue: EU Region login API errors. On September 10 our monitoring detected elevated errors with the Auth API in the EU region.

issue: Cross Transaction Risk (CTR) Instability - ALL DC.

solution: Issue Start: Issue Resolved: The feature is now fully restored and operating as intended.
