issue: Copilot experienced degraded availability for the majority of the features.

issue: Propagation delay in server SDKs.

issue: We are investigating a problem with authorizations. Updates to follow. Downtime: Total downtime was just over an hour.

issue: Provisioning invite links are not working.

issue: Issue with Money Manager Insights.

issue: Copilot Code Review experienced a service degradation that caused 46.97% of pull request review requests to fail, requiring users to re-request a review.
root_cause: The degradation was caused by elevated response times in an internal, model-backed dependency, which led to request timeouts and backpressure in the review processing pipeline, resulting in sustained queue growth and failed review completion.
solution: We mitigated the issue by temporarily bypassing fix suggestions to reduce latency, increasing worker capacity to drain the backlog, and rolling out a model configuration change that reduced end-to-end latency.

issue: Upload API Degradation. Summary the Uploadcare platform experienced a significant service disruption affecting the Upload API and REST API subsystems.
root_cause: Root cause The root cause was a resource contention event on Amazon Elastic File System (EFS), aggravated by an observability side-effect. A monitoring agent, executing a metadata-heavy recursive file scan, monopolized the I/O capacity of the shared NFS mount points.
solution: Engineers manually removed approximately 4,000 "orphaned" files that remained on the disk (files where the background job failed during the crash and could not self-heal).

issue: Cloudflare outage on | Cloudflare Blog Skip to content Cloudflare experienced a service outage when a subset of customers who use Cloudflare’s Bring Your Own IP (BYOIP) service saw their routes to the Internet withdrawn via Border Gateway Protocol (BGP).
root_cause: A bug in an automated cleanup task queried the Addressing API incorrectly, causing the system to interpret all BYOIP prefixes as pending deletion and systematically remove them.
solution: Cloudflare engineers reverted the change and prefixes stopped being withdrawn when we began to observe failures. We resolved the incident when we restored all prefix configurations.

issue: This is unfortunately very similar to the outage we experienced in 2020, on which you can read more on our blog.
root_cause: An automated routing policy configuration error removed prefix list filters from BGP export policies in Cloudflare's Miami router, causing it to advertise internal IPv6 prefixes to external peers and resulting in a route leak lasting 25 minutes.
solution: This was purposeful, as we previously forwarded some IPv6 traffic through Miami toward the Bogotá data center, but recent infrastructure upgrades removed the need for us to do so.

issue: Document Reports not being processed in US. Summary around 10 minutes after restoring service in the EU and CA from the - outage, we go alerted for high error rate in the US region and we noticed the new ML model version was back online in that region.
root_cause: Root Causes A previously rolled back version of an ML model went back live automatically in the US region. The automated canary reversal did not succeed in that region, leaving the deployment in an inconsistent state.
solution: As a result, the model routing labels were not updated as expected during the next forced deployment, and traffic continued to be served by pods running the incorrect model version until we manually rolled back the model in the cluster.

issue: Delays in Document report processing (all Regions). The service unavailability resulted in increased Turnaround Time (TaT) for all Document reports and Studio Autofill created.

Subsequently, the canary release for the application layer failed to progress due to high error rate and automatically reverted both the application and model layer reverting the service to a healthy state.

solution: Upon removing this limit at the impact of high Redis CPU utilization was mitigated, with CPU utilization falling to 5% for the affected node where it had been at 50% prior to the incident. Changes we've made These are the changes we’ve made in response to this incident: Removed the global rate limit that was contributing to a significant proportion of load Increased the number of read replicas for our customer information database to 3 and increased the instance size We’ve reviewed our remaining rate limits and have confirmed that no other rate limits apply globally to all shards.

Next Steps We assess the risk of a similar recurrence as low as the following actions are being understaken.The specific code path that caused this incident has already been reverted, and we are implementing structural safeguards so that this general class of issue cannot recur, regardless of where in the codebase it might otherwise occur.

issue: Issues with Box Shuttle Standalone.
root_cause: Analysis A misconfiguration in Shuttle resulted in depleted resources that accessed job history. This caused Shuttle pages that load job history to time out.
solution: After we restored service, we confirmed that customers could access existing jobs and create new ones. We restored access by restarting the affected services.

issue: Harness Artifact Registry upload is failing from pipeline - EU1 region.
root_cause: Root Cause The component responsible for handling pipeline-based artifact uploads is distributed as a container image.
solution: Because of how that replication was triggered, it copied the original (earlier) image associated with that version label rather than the corrected one. This meant the EU1 cluster — which pulls from the internal mirror — ended up running a different, defective image than other clusters, which pull directly from the public source and therefore received the corrected image.

issue: UI dashboards are lagging behind (CI).
root_cause: Root cause Harness maintains a change-data-capture component that continuously replicates pipeline execution records from the primary operational datastore into a separate time-series datastore optimised for dashboards and reporting queries.
solution: Every affected record remained durably stored and was replayed into the analytics datastore once the underlying limitation was removed.

issue: Querying issues. This timeout was not properly communicated back to the lambda, and while with classic lambdas the task would automatically cut off at 15 minutes, the new LMIs were not enforcing this sort of safety mechanism.
root_cause: First, we have been introducing Lambda Managed Instances (LMI) into our query architecture, which behave similar to classic lambdas in many ways and had been introduced as part of work around querying performance improvements with the goal of a better and faster user experience.
solution: The system recovered by CT, 20 minutes later, when the large queries cleared out, but we continued to investigate the cause of the incident.

issue: Interruption to Programmatic Vanta Agent Installations. We have resolved an issue where customers were unable to programmatically install the Vanta agent using our installation scripts (such as deployments via MDM).
root_cause: This was caused by an unexpected permissions change that made the scripts repository private starting.
solution: Full access has been restored, and scripted installations are now functioning normally.

issue: Incident with Copilot AI Model Providers. users of the Fable 5 model in GitHub Copilot experienced increased request failures and latency.
root_cause: This was caused by degradation of an upstream model provider. The affected endpoint recovered, and we monitored the service until error rates and latency returned to normal levels.
solution: The degradation affecting Copilot AI Model Providers has been mitigated.

issue: Home Depot API Performance Degradation.
root_cause: We observed degraded performance again and the team has identified the issue.
solution: We deployed a fix that should resolve the issue.

issue: Databricks courses may fail to load.
root_cause: Due to an upstream Microsoft Azure Databricks service disruption, some Databricks sessions are slow to start, stuck loading, or failing to launch.
solution: The upstream Azure Databricks issue appears to have cleared and Databricks exercise environments are provisioning normally again.

issue: Inbound connection failure to Fly Apps.
root_cause: A BGP misconfiguration while provisioning new edge capacity caused most traffic from Europe endpoints to be dropped.
solution: The misconfiguration has been fixed and we are implementing safeguards against this kind of issue in the future.

issue: Incident with Copilot. On 2026-08-03, some GitHub Copilot users experienced errors when using chat and agent features.
root_cause: The incident was caused by an increase in how often clients requested the model list, which pushed an internal user-authorization lookup past a rate limit; the rate-limited responses were surfaced to users as errors.
solution: We mitigated the impact by increasing how long Copilot caches that authorization lookup, which reduced load on the internal service, and we have additional capacity and rate-limit changes in progress. The degradation affecting Copilot has been mitigated.

issue: Impossible to vault payment instrument when credit cart option is disabled in the PayPal Commerce and BigCommerce Payments integrations.
root_cause: Commerce Engineers have found the root cause of this issue for both the PayPal Commerce and BigCommerce Payments integrations, and are developing a fix.
solution: Commerce Engineers are investigating an issue impacting PayPal Account Vaulted instrument creation when the Credit Cards feature is disabled in the PayPal Commerce and BigCommerce Payments integrations.

issue: Issues with Uploads and Downloads. On some customers experienced failures and delays when uploading files to Box.
root_cause: The problem was caused by a routing issue on our frontend load balancers.
solution: We restored service by rerouting upload traffic and provisioning additional capacity. Our engineering team mitigated the impact by redirecting traffic away from the affected region, which restored normal upload operations and resolved the errors.

issue: Editing 'Variable Sets' in the IaCM module is experiencing issue. Executive Summary IST, customers using Infrastructure as Code Management (IaCM) on Prod0 and Prod1 were unable to access the Variable Sets settings page.
root_cause: Root Cause A platform routing change released on updated how IaCM settings pages are resolved in the user interface.
solution: We deployed a hotfix that restored full access to the Variable Sets page on Prod0 and Prod1 the same evening, and we are implementing permanent safeguards described below to prevent this class of issue from recurring.

issue: SAT Account Settings not Loading. On Tuesday, some customers experienced issues loading the Account Settings page in the KnowBe4 console across the CA, DE, EU, UK, and US regions.
root_cause: This issue was caused by a series of application changes that increased the complexity of a GraphQL request used by the Account Settings experience.
solution: To prevent this issue in the future, we have increased the complexity threshold.

issue: System Errors in EU-CENTRAL-2.
root_cause: On 4 August 2026, Wasabi S3 services in our Frankfurt (eu-central-2) region were unavailable due to a recent software update to our frontend infrastructure.
solution: The updated was rolled back and services were fully restored on the region.

issue: Issues affecting multiple Box services. and again some customers may have experienced intermittent disruptions affecting login, uploads/downloads, Notes, Box AI, and API access in Box.
root_cause: Analysis We recently introduced automatic capacity scaling to help Box respond more efficiently to changes in customer traffic.
solution: We restored service by increasing capacity and adjusting our systems to better handle traffic under load.

issue: Incident with Actions. on August 7, GitHub Actions experienced degraded availability.
root_cause: The incident was triggered by a routine deployment to an internal Actions service responsible for processing events and generating Actions jobs.
solution: As pods were replaced during the deployment, remaining capacity became saturated, causing services to crash and triggering a cascading impact across multiple clusters and downstream services. This second stage of impact was mitigated by deploying changes to prevent runners from repeatedly attempting to acquire invalid jobs.

issue: Monitoring - Pipelines Stuck - Prod2. As each pass consumed progressively more memory and CPU without ever completing, the service instance performing that work stopped making progress, and every execution assigned to that instance stalled — which is what customers reported.
root_cause: Root Cause Harness pipelines support expressions that are resolved at runtime — for example, an expression that inserts the contents of the Git webhook payload that triggered the pipeline.
solution: Harness engineers identified the cause, mitigated the impact, and pipeline executions returned to normal operation. The majority of pipelines on Prod2 continued to execute successfully throughout the incident; the primary impact was that some in-flight executions could not complete and needed to be re-run once the issue was mitigated.

issue: Delayed sync in integrations.
root_cause: We identified an issue where some third-party integrations were showing disconnected / invalid-token behavior related to the rollout.
solution: The team reverted the change in production and retriggered syncs to recover affected integrations. In those cases, tokens were already revoked, expired, or deactivated, and customers may need to reconnect manually A fix has been deployed and we are rolling it out for all impacted integrations.

issue: Certn Integration Unavailable.
root_cause: A small number of accounts remain impacted and we're continuing to work with Certn to restore them Our Certn Assessment integration is currently unavailable due to an unexpected connection issue with Certn.
solution: Certn has restored access for most affected accounts.

issue: Offer Letter Conversion outage. Incident Summary ET, some customers were unable to send offer letters, and some document and resume previews failed to generate.
root_cause: Root Cause A third-party service we use to convert documents into PDFs experienced an outage lasting most of the day.
solution: We also corrected a related defect that had prevented the backup from being used reliably.

issue: Lucidworks Platform and Search Service Disruption.
root_cause: Root Cause A recent code change to the backend service that manages customer integrations with a third-party authentication and authorization provider altered how that service checked for outdated integrations across a customer's full set of applications.
solution: We disabled the cleanup job on August 7 to stop further disruptions, rotated credentials for confirmed impacted customers, and deployed a permanent fix on August 12. No further customer-facing errors have been detected since the fix was deployed.

issue: Disruption with Copilot for access to some models. GitHub Copilot users saw an incomplete list of available models.
root_cause: The issue was caused by a change to how model data was published, which our systems could not read back correctly and fell back to a limited default list.
solution: We mitigated the incident deployed a fix to prevent immediate recurrence. The issue has been mitigated across all affected environments.

issue: Disruption with creation of fine grained personal access tokens. users were unable to create new fine-grained personal access tokens (FG PAT) through the GitHub website.
root_cause: We identified the source of the issue affecting creation of fine-grained personal access tokens and have applied a mitigation.
solution: GitHub mitigated the incident by disabling the change at which point token creation recovered immediately, and the incident was resolved.

issue: Metrics: Elevated Error Rates Reads/Writes.
root_cause: We experienced elevated error rates for metrics reads and writes due to a networking issue. Impact was limited to a subset of deployments in the prod-us-central-0 region.
solution: A fix has been applied and error rates have since recovered.

issue: Ticketing Service Disruption. We experienced a brief disruption affecting ticketing within the PSA platform.
root_cause: The issue originated in the billing platform service and was resolved within a few minutes after the service was cycled.
solution: We are conducting a review to identify and address the root cause and to prevent recurrence.

issue: Batch SaaS AU - Partial Degradation.
root_cause: We identified an issue that caused degraded performance in our Batch SaaS AU region between -. Customers may see delays processing some of the jobs.
solution: Our team has restored service to normal performance levels.

issue: Billing and Usage Temporarily Unavailable.
root_cause: Due to a degradation of application performance, the Billing and Usage page was temporarily unavailable for all regions.
solution: Billing and usage has been restored to normal functionality.

issue: Incident with GraphQL API Requests. the GraphQL API service was degraded and customers in saw higher than normal timeouts.
root_cause: This was due to increased utilization at one of our sites which caused resource contention across our dependencies, leading to an increase in timeouts for GraphQL requests.
solution: We mitigated the incident by increasing capacity to alleviate the capacity bottleneck. We have identified and mitigated increased error rates affecting GraphQL API requests.

issue: Disruption with Login and Release Asset downloads. There were three windows of impact: (1) August 12, with an average error rate of 16.16% that peaked at 28.6%; (2) August 12, with an average error rate of 16.55% that peaked %; and (3) August 13, with an average error rate of 2.01% that peaked %.
root_cause: On August 12 and 13, 2026, some anonymous (logged-out) requests to github.com experienced HTTP 5xx errors when loading pages like the sign-in page, and when downloading release assets, due to an unusual traffic pattern that repeatedly overloaded a part of our infrastructure that serves these types of requests.
solution: We mitigated the incidents by applying traffic controls at our network edge that limited any requests matching the pattern identified previously, thereby preventing overload on our systems. Errors on the login page and downloading release assets have decreased, but we are not fully mitigated.

issue: Incident with Pull Requests and Issues.
root_cause: We identified the source of errors affecting Pull Requests, Issues, and Search on GitHub.com and have applied a mitigation.
solution: During a database migration, two indexes were removed while application settings still referenced them, causing affected requests to fail. We restored service by disabling both settings.

issue: INC-1104Imperva Management Portal Configuration Changes Issue. In the event of a service disruption, the update will include potential impacts to any affected region.
root_cause: During our ongoing monitoring, we observed another instance of delayed configuration publishing.
solution: The technical team has applied a fix to address the issue, and the Publisher has returned to normal operation.

issue: Lever Outage. Incident Summary the Lever platform experienced partial unavailability.
root_cause: Root Cause The incident was triggered by a safety mechanism within an internal administrative tool designed to prevent expensive database queries.
solution: Resolution Engineering teams identified and terminated the long-running diagnostic operations, which immediately restored database performance and platform stability.

issue: Service Issue - Linode Kubernetes Engine Enterprise (LKE-E)- IAD2 (Washington).
root_cause: Our investigation revealed that while total physical hardware capacity in IAD2 was sufficient, the provisioning request triggered an entitlement check failure due to an initial soft host-allocation threshold.
solution: Full deployment capabilities were restored and stabilized.

issue: Higher ambient temperature in the Phoenix DC. Upon receipt of a formal RFO from RadiusDC, we will distribute a phoenixNAP RFO with further details to our customer base in response to today's outage.
root_cause: This follows an elevated white space temperature issue in the facility, caused by multiple utility bump events which affected the facility's chillers and can be attributed to storms in the Phoenix, Arizona area earlier today.
solution: We are happy to report that as of 11 PM MST our support is once again operational and all systems restored. Some services have been restored, and our teams are continuing to work to bring additional services back online.

issue: Global Errors and Failures with Publish and Functions, Delays with Events & Actions. Customers may have experienced increased publish error rates, delayed or missed message delivery, delayed message persistence, and increased latency for Functions and Events & Actions workflows.
root_cause: The root cause of the incident was an unusually large concentration of global publish traffic that was not limited by our throttling layers.
solution: We mitigated the issue by adjusting targeted traffic controls, increasing capacity for affected publish and replication components, and isolating the high-volume traffic pattern to reduce broader platform impact.

issue: 401 errors due to JWT rejections. We continue to monitor progress and are slowly updating each region.
root_cause: We continue to monitor the fixes introduced by this latest rollout. If you are continuing to see these errors, some customers have reported that restarting their project after the rollout resolved this issue.
solution: We have seen reports that the JWT rejection issue persisted with 14.17, and due to some unintended performance side effects, we have rolled back to Postgrest 14.5. This fix has been applied to the following regions: ap-east-1 ap-northeast-1 ap-northeast-2 ap-south-1 ap-southeast-1 ap-southeast-2 ca-central-1 eu-central-1 eu-central-2 eu-north-1 eu-west-2 eu-west-3 We will continue rolling out this fix to the remaining regions throughout this week and provide updates as more regions are successful.

issue: Platform: Unable to Launch New PRA Sessions in Non-US Regions. Incident Overview A subset of customers in non-US regions were unable to launch new PRA sessions and received an "Engine unavailable" error.
root_cause: Start, End, Root Cause and Remediation A new version of the PRA service was deployed to production. The new version did not correctly apply a required configuration value in the production environment, which prevented the service from locating the session engine for non-US regions.
solution: Following an increase in backend error rates during post-deployment monitoring, correlated with incoming customer reports, the deployment was rolled back to the previous stable version.

issue: Delayed Email Deliverability.
root_cause: Email delivery was delayed due to an issue with an upstream email service provider. This affected customers who have not yet configured a custom email domain or a custom email provider.
solution: We've mitigated the impact and email delivery is returning to normal.

issue: Incident with GitHub.com. from – (7h 47m), GitHub.com experienced elevated errors and latency across Issues, Pull Requests, APIs, Actions, and Copilot.
root_cause: The immediate cause of the failure was network saturation on load balancers in Central US due to a new peak in traffic.
solution: We have partially disabled authentication token retries and have seen improvement, and we are monitoring impact before fully applying this mitigation. The degradation affecting Git Operations has been mitigated.

issue: Investigating reports of failed SIP Transfer calls in US East. Automated monitoring detects the elevated failure rate and our team begins investigating.
root_cause: Root Cause The configuration change restarts the servers that handle SIP signaling one at a time.
solution: Before a server is shut down, it is removed from service so that no new calls reach it, and it is then given some time to finish the calls it is already handling. We are changing our rollout process so that a server which cannot be removed from service safely halts the rollout.

issue: Inbound Twilio calls experiencing intermittent connection failures. Affected callers were unable to connect to an agent; outbound calls and other traffic were unaffected.
root_cause: A small percentage (<1%) of inbound Twilio calls failed to connect due to a configuration error on our side.
solution: The change has been rolled back and calls have been connecting normally since.

issue: Intermittent failures in runner group and runner-related permissions pages. customers were unable to view or manage Actions Runners and Runner Groups through the GitHub UI and API.
root_cause: The issue was caused by failures in backend requests reading runner and runner group data. The failures were caused by an expired authentication certificate unique to this service.
solution: The impact was mitigated by completing the enablement of the new certificate in the backend system. We have added additional monitoring to this and other certificates.

issue: Incident with Actions. customers were unable to run jobs on Actions Larger Runners and were unable to view or manage Actions Runners and Runner Groups through the GitHub UI and API.
root_cause: These issues were caused by failures in backend requests resolving essential metadata for starting Larger Runner workflow runs and for reading runner and runner group data.
solution: We mitigated the issues by completing the enablement of the new certificate in the backend system. We have added additional monitoring to this and other certificates.

issue: PAB sending a Non-Delivery Report after an Email is Reported (US Only).
root_cause: This issue was caused by a configuration change to the shared email routing infrastructure. This change renamed a messaging component used by both our staging and production environments.
solution: To prevent this type of issue in the future, we are separating email routing configurations for our staging and production environments.

issue: Atlas UI and API Periodic Unavailability.
root_cause: Following the incident, we identified an issue that caused some internal Atlas jobs not to start as scheduled, resulting in delays to certain changes.
solution: The issue was related to this incident "Atlas UI and API Periodic Unavailability" which has been remediated. We have disabled the workload and are monitoring the situation We have identified a new workload that was putting more load than expected on the backing system.

issue: Paxos - Crypto Transfers Incident Detected.
root_cause: We identified an issue with internal blockchain event processing that caused a subset of deposits to be missed by our normal processing workflow.
solution: The change has been rolled back and normal deposit processing has been restored.

issue: Monad RPC elevated error rates.
root_cause: We identified an issue causing elevated error rates for Monad RPC requests.
solution: Our team has deployed a fix, and error rates have returned to normal.

issue: Issue with Microsoft Office Integration and Box Edit. on some users may have experienced difficulties while working in Box.
root_cause: The deployment introduced a regression that caused the service’s performance to degrade under peak load, which led to client timeouts and errors.
solution: We restored functionality by reverting the deployment to a previous version.

issue: Data ingestion is delayed on Traceable US production. Summary On 19 August 2026, the Harness Application Security service experienced a significant disruption affecting both the customer-facing console and the data ingestion pipeline in the SaaS Production and US1 regions.
root_cause: Root Cause The internal configuration service that supplies runtime settings to nearly every other component became overloaded and entered a repeated restart cycle.
solution: Disabling the new feature in both affected regions restored throughput sharply and durably. The feature that triggered this incident remains disabled and will not be re-enabled until the work below is complete and validated.

issue: Quickbooks Online Latency Issue. Earlier today, some users experienced issues with QuickBooks Online (QBO) features.
root_cause: Our engineering team is actively investigating the issue to identify the root cause and restore normal performance as quickly as possible.
solution: All services are now restored and functioning normally.

issue: FME API write operations started returning 499 errors. Because 499 is a valid, expected response in that deny path, the failures did not look like an outage on our alerts, and the incident was identified from customer reports rather than internal detection.
root_cause: Status: Root Cause A change in how a shared governance service authenticated inbound calls resulted in some FME writes being rejected.
solution: The issue was mitigated by reverting a recent authentication change in a shared governance service, and affected writes returned to normal. Remediation Reverted the governance-service authentication change.

issue: Investigating reports of elevated egress & connector API errors. We added disruption protection for the affected service and are continuing broader resilience improvements.
root_cause: Root Cause An internal routing service lost one of its two instances, and a concurrent infrastructure issue with our cloud provider was preventing new compute nodes from provisioning in US East, so the replacement couldn't start.
solution: An automated maintenance process removed that last instance, making the service fully unavailable.

issue: Duplicate deliveries for a small percentage of iOS transaction events.
root_cause: Between August 17 and August 20, a defect caused some iOS subscription transactions to be duplicated under more than one user profile.
solution: Duplicated records have been removed — dashboards and exports now show corrected figures, and per-user payment summaries have been recalculated. The defect is disabled and no new duplicates are being created.

issue: Degraded Git Operations over SSH. dotcom Git operations over SSH were degraded.
root_cause: The incident was caused by a software defect in our load-balancing infrastructure that was triggered by a configuration change.
solution: We mitigated the incident by rolling back the configuration change.

issue: PAB | Error Reporting Phish using Gmail Phish Alert Button. On Friday, some customers experienced intermittent failures when using the Gmail Phish Alert Button add-in to report suspicious emails, receiving the "An internal error has occurred" message instead of a successful report confirmation.
root_cause: This issue was caused by a disruption in a caching service on Google's Apps Script platform, which the add-in relies store per-user session configuration.
solution: Error volume declined sharply shortly after as the vendor-side condition cleared, and the Gmail Phish Alert Button returned to normal performance.

issue: Edge Delivery Issues in India.
root_cause: After further investigation the issue appears to not be caused by a third-party service provider. We are working with the service provider and actively investigating the issue and will provide another update within the next 60 minutes.
solution: We can confirm that the issue was mitigated the service has resumed normal operation.

issue: Feature Management & Experimentation (FME) user interface unavailable. Summary Starting at several FME customers reported failures loading the FME UI.
root_cause: FME UI Artifacts served from the CDN expired due to a retention policy, causing FME UI to fail to load. Any flag request changes through the API, change delivery, and the data pipeline continued to work with no interruption.
solution: SDK functionality and runtime flag evaluation Admin API calls Customer flag configuration data No data loss occurred Remediation FME UI got restored in the CDN through a deployment Recovery confirmed across all production environments before closing the incident.

issue: Issue with Downloads. Between some Box Zones Japan users may have had a degraded download experience.
root_cause: The disruption was caused by an unusual traffic pattern that placed unexpected strain on capacity in the region.
solution: Once the impact was identified we restored service by directing download traffic to another region and adding capacity.

issue: Data Processing Delays - Activity Page and Reports Affected.
root_cause: The Activity Page and Reports on the Helios platform may show delayed or stale information due to an unplanned background sync issue.
solution: We have deployed a fix, and the sync is expected to complete within the next six hours.

issue: Actions delays in starting runs. In this case, although the node was severely degraded and unable to perform disk operations, it continued sending healthy signals, preventing the system from immediately moving its work elsewhere.
root_cause: The incident was caused by a disk failure on a node hosting one of many service instances responsible for processing runner assignment events.
solution: Typically, pods on unhealthy nodes are removed and replaced automatically without impact. The queue backlog was cleared and processing returned to normal.

issue: Elevated errors on Fable 5 due to upstream provider. Users encountered elevated error rates when using Claude Fable 5, with requests sometimes failing mid-response.
root_cause: On August 24th, 2026, the Copilot service experienced a degradation of the Claude Fable 5 model due to an issue with our upstream provider.
solution: The issue was resolved by a mitigation put in place by our provider.

issue: Email delivery failure affecting sign-up verification and notification emails. We are re-sending sign-up verification and password reset emails that failed to deliver during the incident window (August 22, CDT through today).
root_cause: Emails sent by LaunchDarkly — including sign-up verification, password reset, teammate invitation, and workflow notification emails — are currently failing to deliver due to an authentication issue with an upstream email delivery provider.
solution: Once delivery is restored, we will re-send affected verification and password reset emails.

issue: Agent session analytics displaying incorrect values in EU Central and India regions.
root_cause: We identified an issue where agent session analytics in the Cloud dashboard displayed zero concurrent sessions, beginning late on August.
solution: Some gaps may remain in historical data from the affected window (August 21–24 ); these will be backfilled. Ingestion has been restored and we are backfilling historical analytics for the affected window; some charts may show incomplete history until this completes.

issue: Spike in Visual Authenticity failures on Facial Similarity Motion randomness checks. 24 August: a customer reported a drop in workflow success rates and we began investigating.
root_cause: Root Causes A stricter validation of the motion randomness challenge was being trialled with a single customer, controlled by a per-customer configuration setting.
solution: Disabling the change restored normal clear rates immediately. 25 August: we reverted the change and clear rates returned to normal within minutes.

issue: Buildkite service disruption. Service Impact Customers experienced a site-wide disruption affecting the Buildkite web interface, REST API, Agent API, job queue, and notifications.
root_cause: During post-incident analysis we discovered some bugs and gaps in our monitoring of CoreDNS, particularly around query volume and duration.
solution: Pending requests accumulated in memory, until all three original CoreDNS pods exceeded their allowed memory limits and were restarted by Kubernetes.

issue: Unexpected agent disconnection for some customers.
root_cause: At we deployed a defective request routing change to agent-edge.buildkite.com, which caused some customers' agents to abruptly disconnect.
solution: At we noticed the problem, and immediately reverted the change.

issue: Potential delays to SEK, NOK & DKK.
root_cause: Root Cause A payment processing service encountered an unexpected condition that prevented new payment submissions from being processed for a short period of time.
solution: The issue was identified and mitigated the same day, with full service stability confirmed following additional monitoring. Client Impact A limited number of SEK, NOK and DKK payments experienced a one day delay, while the vast majority of payments were processed on the intended value date after service was restored.

issue: Query performance degradation in Azure Westeurope.
root_cause: We discovered the stalled partition required manual intervention to complete initialization. One half of the partition remained online to serve queries and writes while its companion half was impaired.
solution: Recovery actions The team allocated additional query resources, then manually inspected and restarted the impaired partition after identifying the incomplete recovery. Impaired partition was manually inspected and restarted.

issue: Service degradation due to network connectivity issue in Southeast Asia.
root_cause: A subset of Optimizely customers may experience connectivity issues or service degradation in the Southeast Asia region due to a network connectivity issue reported by our third-party provider.
solution: The third‑party provider has mitigated the issue.

issue: Potential for some missed messages for subscribers in US East PoP.
root_cause: Root Cause During planned internal load testing, a group of internal routing servers was removed from service.
solution: A rolling restart of the affected servers cleared the outdated addresses.

issue: Intermittent Cell Link and Cross Sheet Reference delays/failures.
root_cause: The root cause was an asynchronous calculation change that performed partial data loads, omitting dependent cells and silently persisting inaccurate formula values.
solution: The issue was mitigated on August 27 at by disabling the optimization flags, with full data restoration completed on August 28 after recalculating approximately all affected known sheets. Engineering mitigated the propagation by blocking the problematic source sheet.

issue: System Errors in US-EAST-1.
root_cause: Earlier today, some customers in our US-EAST-1 region may have experienced elevated latency or errors on storage PUT requests due to an internal infrastructure issue on our backend.
solution: Our team identified the cause and applied a fix.

issue: Engine scaling issues in Dremio Cloud (US).
root_cause: The issue was caused by an infrastructure artifact required for engine provisioning being inadvertently removed during a compliance-related infrastructure change.
solution: Our team identified the root cause, restored the affected component across all US regions, and confirmed that engine operations returned to normal.

issue: Disruption with GitHub Billing. on August 27, GitHub Billing experienced degraded performance affecting billing budget pages and GitHub Copilot CLI sessions.
root_cause: We confirmed this impact for a small number of customers ( This was caused by a concentrated workload that created processing delays in our data storage layer.
solution: We mitigated the incident by rebalancing traffic within our infrastructure.

issue: Incident with Actions and Pull Requests. Background jobs that process pull request updates and generate merge commits were impacted by timeouts reaching a single partition of git data.
root_cause: 2.6% of workflow runs triggered by pull request events were delayed, with the impact rising as high as 25% at its peak.
solution: We reduced workload, shifted traffic away from affected infrastructure, and restored the affected service component to a healthy state. The degradation affecting Actions and Pull Requests has been mitigated.

issue: Incident with Actions. This ramp was deliberately slow to ensure we did not re-overwhelm the system given our original throttling was now known to be incorrectly set.
root_cause: This impact was triggered by saturation of writes to the database primary used by the service processing triggers for Actions workflows.
solution: The primary was failed over, but the system did not fully recover. The degradation affecting Actions has been mitigated.

issue: Degraded Query API Performance impacting US Projects. Mixpanel RCA: Temporary Query Service Disruption for US Projects Summary PT projects in the US region experienced failures loading reports and running queries through the Mixpanel UI and Query API.
root_cause: Root cause identified; recovery efforts began on the first affected server group.
solution: All events continued to be collected and stored normally throughout the incident; once query service was restored, all reports reflected complete, accurate data with no customer action required. Service was restored, the impacted servers were brought back online, and the internal tooling was disabled.

issue: Issues accessing multiple Atlassian products in some regions. The incident caused service disruption to customer traffic originating from Western Europe and Southeast APAC regions, with HTTP 404 errors returned.
root_cause: ROOT CAUSE The event was triggered by a code change to one of our proxy fleets.
solution: The incident was detected within 1 minute by our automated monitoring systems, and mitigated by rolling back to the previous configuration release, which put the proxy fleet into a known good state. Once the proxy fleet functionality was restored, the surge of traffic overwhelmed the Jira service tier, which returned an elevated rate of HTTP 503s until it automatically scaled out again.

issue: Incident with Copilot AI Model Providers. Users encountered elevated error rates when using Kimi K3.
root_cause: On August 27th, 2026, the Copilot service experienced a degradation of the Kimi K3 model due to an issue with our upstream provider.
solution: The issue was resolved by a mitigation put in place by our provider. The issues with our upstream model provider have been mitigated, and Kimi K3 is once again available in Copilot products and IDE surfaces.

issue: Unexpected HTTP response code affecting login, sheet access, Control Center, Dynamic View and other premium apps. Between August 26, customers experienced intermittent issues logging in to Smartsheet and loading sheets, Dashboards, Reports, and certain premium applications, including Control Center, Dynamic View, WorkApps, and Resource Management.
root_cause: On August 28, at we identified the true root cause — the feature-setting change — and deployed a permanent fix by that corrected the underlying defect, fully resolving the issue across all regions.
solution: Our engineering teams responded quickly by adding capacity to the affected systems on August 26, which restored access by that same day.

issue: Resolved: intermittent TRM login issues.
root_cause: The issue was caused by an intermittent outage affecting one of our authentication service providers.
solution: The provider restored service, and TRM login access has been restored and validated Some customers and internal users were intermittently unable to log in to TRM for approximately 38 minutes on 27 August 2026. The provider has restored service, and TRM login access has been restored and validated.

issue: Entities in Harness are not loading on in Prod3. Summary Between August 27, customers experienced an issue where some pipelines, deployments, and related resources appeared as not found in the Harness UI and API, even though the underlying data remained intact.
root_cause: Root Cause The issue was caused by a configuration error introduced during a planned internal service routing update in Production.
solution: Engineering identified the issue, rolled back the change, and restored normal service. The issue was limited to the affected production environment and was resolved by reverting the change and restoring the previous service communication path.

issue: Service Issue - US-SEA (Seattle, WA).

issue: Platform: Login Failures and Degraded Performance. Incident Overview Delinea Platform customers in the US region experienced intermittent login failures and slow performance when signing in or accessing their tenants, including error or timeout pages on the sign-in screen for some users.
root_cause: Start: approximately End: approximately Root Cause and Remediation A caching related code change that was made on Aug 27, combined with an unusually large volume of background synchronization activity on Aug 28, exceeded the normal operating capacity of our caching infrastructure supporting login and authentication services.
solution: Our engineering team rolled back the caching change and restarted the affected services, which cleared the failed connections and began restoring functionality, though performance remained degraded. The caching resource was scaled up to restore normal performance.

issue: Some Customers Experiencing Payment Failures and Processing Delays for CAD. Overview On 31 August 2026 and 1 September 2026, some customers experienced payment failures and processing delays affecting payments routed through one of our banking partners.
root_cause: The issue was caused by a disruption within our liquidity funding process, which resulted in a temporary funding shortfall and prevented certain payments from being processed as expected.
solution: Corrective actions were implemented to restore normal payment processing, and the incident was resolved on 1 September 2026 following confirmation that funding balances had been corrected and payment operations had returned to normal service Client Impact A subset of customers experienced payment failures or delays during the incident period. No customer funds were lost as a result of this incident, and normal payment processing was restored following corrective action.

solution: The incident was identified and service was restored on 1 September 2026. The issue was identified and resolved by updating the service configuration to use the intended platform routing mechanism.

issue: Delays in commit processing.
root_cause: The incident was caused by a sharp, concentrated surge in push volume that saturated worker pools and job queueing infrastructure.
solution: The incident was mitigated by manually scaling the affected worker pools and increasing push-processing capacity.

issue: Web SDK Outage (all regions).
root_cause: Root Causes A routine update to a container image for our document configuration service introduced a regression to the synchronization job that updates the documents list.
solution: _13:44:_ Cause identified and change rolled back.

issue: Increased errors for new render requests. Summary a network fault in a Google Cloud Platform region disrupted connectivity to infrastructure that powers a portion of Imgix's image and video rendering pipeline.
root_cause: Google has confirmed the disruption was caused by an incident that occurred during their network maintenance and is continuing to review the incident.

What We Will Do To Prevent This In The Future We are refining our criteria and procedures for cross-regional traffic shifts to improve our responses in future incidents.

issue: Pipelines are stuck in Prod1. Duration of impact: Approximately 45–50 minutes of degraded graph and status visibility.
root_cause: Root Cause A planned database failover activity in the Prod1 region temporarily increased network latency between the pipeline execution service and its database while traffic was briefly served cross-region.
solution: Harness engineering identified the cause, added processing capacity, and restored normal graph and status updates. As the backlog grew, graph rendering and status updates fell increasingly behind actual execution progress, and some graphs had to be rebuilt rather than served from cache.

issue: Webhook Notification Delivery Delays and Missing Notifications. Overview Between the afternoon of Thursday 3 September 2026 and the evening of Friday 4 September 2026 (UK time), some customers experienced delays receiving webhook notifications from Currencycloud.
root_cause: Root Cause The delay was caused by a performance issue in the database supporting our notification delivery system, which caused it to run under sustained heavy load.
solution: The underlying issue was identified, and a fix was deployed on Friday 4 September 2026, and the resulting backlog was fully cleared by the evening of the same day. Once the fix was deployed and the backlog cleared, the large majority of delayed notifications were delivered automatically with no need for any customer action.

issue: Disruption with Copilot Code Review. Affected pull request reviews failed to complete or post review comments.
root_cause: The incident was caused by a change to the service’s authentication permissions that prevented it from submitting affected reviews to the GitHub API.
solution: We reverted the change and restored normal operation.

issue: Advanced Aggregations — Degraded Performance. Summary On September 4–5, 2026, we experienced an issue affecting Advanced Aggregations in which some customers saw inaccurate aggregation results because recent card transaction data may have been missing.
root_cause: Why it happened The root cause was a data type mismatch: the cards table id values grew beyond the maximum value supported by a 4-byte integer.
solution: After mitigation was deployed, we replayed the queued events and completed a backfill so that aggregations reflected the correct underlying transaction data.

issue: EUR virtual account creation.
root_cause: Root Cause The incident was caused by a failure within an internal message-processing component responsible for transferring Virtual Account creation requests between systems.
solution: Once service was restored, all queued requests were processed successfully and normal account creation resumed. Restarting the affected component restored normal processing and allowed all queued requests to be completed.

issue: Prod2 was intermittently unavailable.

solution: Remediation Immediate: We have added additional monitoring and increased resources for handling the influx of traffic.

issue: Identified increased agent join latencies in eu-central. Newly provisioned servers failed to start, so the region could not add capacity.
root_cause: Root Cause A configuration change introduced a formatting error in the startup settings for the server pools that run hosted agents in our eu-central region.
solution: Agents that were already running were unaffected, but new agent deployments, version rollouts, and automatic scale-ups were delayed or stuck pending until the change was reverted. We identified the malformed startup configuration and reverted the change.

Our engineering team restarted the affected authentication services, which released the accumulated connections and restored login functionality.

issue: DBDevOps Builds Failing intermittently. Summary on Wednesday, some customers running Database DevOps pipelines in Production experienced intermittent failures when executing schema migration steps (for example Apply Schema and related Database DevOps steps).
root_cause: Root Cause This issue required two separate problems to occur together. First, pipeline plan creation runs on a shared pool of background worker threads, and each thread can handle work for many different customer accounts over time.
solution: Remediation Immediate: Rolled back the Database DevOps service change that enforced the stricter account-binding validation in the most impacted Production environment, restoring Database DevOps pipeline execution for affected customers.

issue: KSAT - Unable to Login (US Only). After hitting a platform execution limit, the job was terminated and automatically retried five times in 15-minute intervals, resulting in a 75-minute outage.
root_cause: Root Cause An unbounded, single-transaction background job for large-group user archival held exclusive locks on many affected rows, blocking the login process's own row write.
solution: To resolve the issue, we deployed a fix that decoupled logins from the lock. When the job reached a 15-minute platform execution limit, it was terminated mid-transaction, the transaction rolled back, and the job was redelivered to the queue.

solution: Recovery and communication Responders restarted affected application instances, which triggered reconnection to the healthy Redis instance. As connections recovered and queued work drained, error rates and latency returned to normal.

solution: We mitigated the incident by removing the affected server from service after which the queued merge commits were created within six minutes. The degradation affecting Pull Requests has been mitigated.

issue: Dashboard aggregator experiencing timeouts across prod2 since (Sept 21). Summary customers in Prod 2 experienced degraded and then largely unavailable deployment dashboards for approximately three hours.
root_cause: Root Cause The dashboard queries were missing a time-range filter on the column used to split the largest table into weekly segments, so each query read all historical data instead of only the requested period.
solution: A rolling restart of the affected service restored dashboards fully, and the platform has been stable since. As data volume grew, the cost of those reads exceeded what the database could serve, and retries of the failing queries added further load, so the condition did not clear until the service was restarted.

solution: Long-term engineering updates are currently being deployed to ensure provisioning utilities dynamically assign distinct, active DNS resolvers across all regions to prevent recurrence.

root_cause: US Pacific time, we observed an issue impacting All Files Page, Box Notes, API calls, logins and downloads.
solution: Our systems automatically detected and corrected the underlying issue.

issue: CI Linux Cloud VM Networking issues - intermittent. Summary (–) customers using Harness CI self-hosted Linux cloud runners in prod1/prod2 (us-west1) experienced intermittent networking failures during pipeline execution — primarily Git/network timeouts when fetching source code.
root_cause: Root Cause This was primarily due to saturation of our NAT which was futher exacerbated by a temporary cloud provider compute capacity, preventing new VM provisioning there.
solution: Failed to connect to github.com port 443: Connection timed out Remediation Immediate: Rebalanced ARM build-VM load from the saturated us-west1 path toward central1 (partially limited by central1 capacity); restarted the affected Cloud NAT gateways, which stabilized pipeline networking.

issue: Prod2: CV is failing with errors for all customers. Summary Customers on Prod-2 experienced elevated failure rates in Continuous Verification pipelines.
root_cause: This was caused by an unexpected traffic spike to one of our backend systems.
solution: Service was restored by scaling out the affected platform component.

issue: Elevated Errors on US-5 Public Cloud. We've observed that service error rates on the US-5 Public Cloud Environment have subsided and returned to baseline, marking a return to service functionality.
root_cause: Meanwhile, our investigation is continuing and we're collaborating with our third-party provider's technical teams to identify and address the root cause of the issue within their hosted infrastructure.
solution: After monitoring the environment to ensure stability, we observe that services have been restored. The service disruption has been mitigated and we're monitoring the ensure stability.

solution: The incident with Moneris has been resolved successfully and the impacted services are fully restored.

issue: Potential Slowness in BlazeMeter UI. The R&D team is performing some testing on our backend systems that may potentially cause slowness in the BlazeMeter UI.
root_cause: We are monitoring the system and we will return the system to normal functionality if we notice any slowness start to occur due to the testing.
solution: We did observe some brief slowness in the system during the testing, but we have restored the system to normal functionality now.

issue: Investigating Technical Issue: SQS Notifications.
root_cause: A full Root Cause Analysis (RCA) will be provided after our investigation is complete. Between ET and ET some notifications may not have been delivered to partner SQS queues.
solution: The list of impacted notifications has been limited to the following: orders.completed orders.created orders.updated The missed orders.completed notifications will be replayed at approximately ET.

issue: Actions Job Delays. Actions is experiencing degraded performance.
root_cause: A detailed root cause analysis will be shared as soon as it is available. GitHub Actions experienced degraded performance for some hosted runners due to throttling within an upstream Azure dependency.
solution: The degradation affecting Actions has been mitigated.

issue: Degradation of Identity Verification & DocProof Services due to the OCR model instability. Ongoing backlog processing: While real-time transaction processing and error rates have normalized, our backend services continue to process the transaction backlog.
root_cause: Root cause: Our engineering team identified an underlying OCR model issue causing failures in data extraction for ID documents and DocProof transactions, leading to processing delays and unexpected rejections.
solution: Additionally, all backlogged transactions have been cleared, and processing latency has returned to normal levels. Current status & Regional impact: - Errors cleared globally: The elevated error rates and intermittent MISSING_MANDATORY_DATAPOINTS rejections affecting fully automated transactions have now stopped across all data centers, and error rates have returned to normal levels.

issue: Sui Data Delay in Reactor & KYT.
root_cause: The Sui pipeline has been stalled since approximately due to a Sui GRPC specification change.
solution: We manually backfilled 20,000 blocks, and the vast majority of unaffected blocks have been published up to about the last hour.

issue: Website and services partially unavailable due to high database load. The impact of this is that our website and API were partially unavailable (more precisely, at 80-90% availability) during that time.
root_cause: Root cause analysis An internal orchestrator service used to update the state of CI/CD jobs, including build jobs and store submission jobs, was updated to retry upon application-level failures.
solution: Remediation The commit that changed retry behavior was rolled back and we are clearing the queue of retries.

issue: INC-1152 IPv6 connectivity degradation across multiple PoPs.
root_cause: Traffic for WAR has been bypassed to restore service stability while our engineering teams actively investigate the root cause for XSP and the underlying issue at WAR.
solution: Service for Singapore (XSP), Atlanta (ATL), Detroit (DET), and Tokyo (NRT) has been fully restored and is operating normally.
